# Project History

✅ **THR-1066 — two register defects fixed, and the abstraction gate measured rather than obeyed** (2026-08-12, Encounter Experience) — the predicate re-derived from 3 templates to 6 once THR-929 closed, exactly as the ticket warned it would: `social.spy_on` rose 6.22 → 7.58 because an outcome rewrite shortens the denominator, while `ag.senior.deep_expedition` fell below threshold. The two genuine defects were mortal-drawn templates addressing the *mortal* as "you" — the player is a god watching a person, not that person — and house voice was already next door (`ag.senior.bounty_hunt`: *"The guild calls on its sergeants"*). Rewritten to third person; second person 4 → 0 on both, and abstraction fell as a side effect because the removed words were themselves nominalisations, so **both clear every detector with no detector change**. The other four fail on abstraction alone, and the corpus says why: `countAbstractNouns` is a suffix proxy whose own docstring calls it "a **ranking** signal, not a verdict on any single line", yet it gates — failing **128 of 683 templates (18.7%)**, dominated by ones whose subject noun *is* the abstraction (`hod.promotion` takes 10 of 14 hits from `ascension`/`devotion`; `action.flesh.cultivate` scores 13.33). Class-scoping, the THR-1045-shaped fix, was measured and **rejected**: net 7, with 8 templates newly failing. Demoting the gate is what the evidence favours but it redefines "clean" for every future WS5 conversion against the THR-883 locked format, so it is filed with the measurement as [THR-1092](https://linear.app/threadbare/issue/THR-1092/the-abstraction-detector-is-documented-as-a-ranking-signal-but-wired) rather than applied on executor authority — including the trap that demoting would make `aftermath-prose-coverage.test.ts:188` pass vacuously. Mutex on THR-929 reversed on evidence (THR-688 rule B). 992 files / 15886 green, ratchet 3447 unchanged.

Deletion self-pins the ticket's anti-regression Done-when — the field is gone, so a writer cannot type-check without re-adding the type. **The find is the guard underneath:** the invariant that keeps toasts from returning is that the three encounter events carry no `notification` directive (`routeNotifications` skips anything without one), and nothing tested it — while a test asserting the **pre-THR-664** contract (`notification.channel === 'toast'`) had been green for three weeks behind an `if (retinueEvent && …)` guard that stopped matching when the directive was removed. Its entire describe block was inert besides: the fixture filtered town encounters to those absent from the unified pool, which seed-system-v2 reduced to **0 of 74**, and each test opened `if (available.length === 0) return` — three tests, zero assertions executed. All three now run against a real population with the empty-population early-return converted to an assertion. 960 files / 15004 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean, 30-tick smoke at 383 agents / 47 events. Browser pass at 1920×1080: 3 live toasts in-viewport, `childDivCount: 0` (deleted card's root shape absent), `hasSpanBody: true`, aria-labels in the plain-message form, 0 new console errors.
✅ **THR-1005 (partial, parked) — the spent final step of a resolved encounter outranks its own aftermath** (2026-08-06, Encounter Experience) — resumed from the prior pass's checkpoint. That pass hardened `runEncounterAutoOpenScan` to walk past a notification that *declines* and honestly recorded that it changed nothing observable. The blocker it could not clear: **the final step notification of a resolved action does not decline.** `currentStep` freezes at the final index on resolution rather than advancing, so THR-664's `stepIndex === currentStepIndex` check passes for it forever, and nothing marks a spent step notification `resolved`. The aftermath is appended last, directly behind it. Measured live at `?spawn=tg.senior.jewel_heist` by replaying the opener's own predicates: queue `[step0, step1, step2, aftermath]` at `currentStep 2`; steps 0/1 declined, **step 2 did not**, ate the single auto-interrupt slot, aftermath never reached. `isStepNotificationSupersededByAftermath` retires it, scoped to "an aftermath for *this action* is still pending" so a digest-tier or already-acknowledged record cannot be stranded. 7 new tests, injection-proven (`expected 'n_step2' to be 'n_aftermath'`), including one that drives the scan through the *real* opener predicates rather than a stub asserting steps decline — the assumption the prior fixture encoded. **Second find:** `inspectEncounterPipeline('@hero')` has no alias resolution — every filter is a raw substring match on node id/name — so it returns all-zeros for any world state, which is what impediment #447 recorded and the checkpoint promoted to its live lead. Demonstrated at one instant: unfiltered `2 threads / 4 notifications`, `'@hero'` `0 / 0`. Now resolves to the avatar or errors loudly (impediment #449). 960 files / 15011 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean. Browser-verified at 1920×1080: aftermath auto-opens unprompted, no badge click. **Deliberately not closed** — the aftermath renders with and without the fix on this route (the veil keys off the resolved action, not the notification kind), so the Done-when passed before either fix and does not capture the reported symptom; parked for one plain-language question to Christian.

✅ **THR-740 — a comment described the intended state and the code did the opposite** (2026-08-06, Continuous Improvement) — `codexRegistry.ts` declared its own 79-row `ACTION_ART` copy directly beneath a comment claiming it imported the canonical registry. Consolidation was safe to do mechanically because the diff proved the codex copy a strict subset (79 rows against 87, zero unique keys, zero disagreeing paths); the 8 canonical-only keys are legacy bare divine aliases no codex id hits, and they were checked for collision with `ITEM_ART_BASE` since `ACTION_ART` spreads last into `ITEM_ART`. The regression guard is the deliverable: one test asserts exactly one file under `src/` declares `ACTION_ART`, falsified against the pre-fix tree. A verification trap worth carrying forward — the browser probe meant to prove the duplicate gone matched `/ACTION_ART\s*:/` against Vite's *transformed* source, which strips the type annotation, so it read clean for both files (impediment #437).
✅ **THR-1008 — the file:line the ticket named had been unreachable for eighteen days, and the leak it described was live one component over** (2026-08-06, Encounter Experience) — the UI Laws review filed two findings against `ThreadsPanel.tsx`: the Encounter Pool modal rendering `Score 0.42 · completion 65% · travel 0.10`, and a pipe-delimited meta strip. The ticket's own first step was *verify the noun*; doing it found the live twin. `EncounterDecisionPanel` in `ThreadDetailView.tsx` — reached by clicking any thread row — was printing `Viable now: 40`, `Template: encounter.confront_the_unknown`, `Travel cost: 0.5808826068191627`, `Best score: 0.54` and `Funnel: Cached 5544 -> Awareness 3308 -> …`: a raw internal key and a 19-significant-figure float on a player-reachable surface, worse than what was filed. Dead copy deleted (291 lines, five formatters, the state and its render site); the live diagnostics gated behind the designer view, whose module header already stated the rule (*"the player surface must never grow a numbers toggle"*). **The fix that the fix forced:** rank and score were doing double duty — leaking magnitudes *and* being the only thing telling two rows apart, because the pool routinely holds one template at a dozen destinations (nine consecutive identical rows, measured live at tick 6). Removing them alone traded a numeral leak for an undifferentiated wall, so normal play collapses the pool through `groupEncounterPoolCandidates` — the grouping the deleted modal had offered as a view mode, repointed rather than deleted with it — and says how many other places share a template in words. Browser pass at 1920×1080: ten distinct named options, **zero numerals anywhere in the section**, viewport contract held, 0 console errors; flipping the designer view restores every figure. `summarizeEncounterPoolDominance` lost its last caller with the modal — filed as THR-1012 rather than pruned in passing.

✅ **THR-927 — the gate counted claims while protecting an invariant about implementations** (2026-08-03, Continuous Improvement) — `pull-work` Step 1.5 read two issues `In Dev` under the executor and exited 1 as a cross-session leak; both were shipped by the **single** armed PR #1191 carrying `Fixes THR-925` and `Fixes THR-926` on their own lines, waiting only on CI (impediment #365). Open claims and concurrent implementations are the same number only when every PR closes exactly one ticket, which the closeout protocol explicitly does not require. Step 1.5 now resolves each claim to the open PR that closes it and counts only claims resolving to none. Two deliberate deviations from the ticket's proposal: the keyword match is **line-anchored** to match `linear-autoclose.yml` exactly (THR-738), since an unanchored grep would discharge a claim on a mid-sentence mention that will never close it; and discharged claims never gate at any count, because the `docs-only` drain (THR-938) deliberately creates multi-PR boards. The sharpest evidence was that run's own board — one discharged claim plus one genuine in-flight claim would have red-exited the run that fixed it.
✅ **THR-1014 — the probe could not see the run that was never created** (2026-08-07, Continuous Improvement) — Rule 0 pickup, and the condition was still live at claim time. THR-1013 taught the probe a second verdict for a run that hangs; this is the strictly worse case where **no run is created at all**, and it is the one a run-list detector is blind to by construction — a run list that stops growing is indistinguishable from a quiet hour, so the verdict, decided by the newest completed run, reads a stale-but-clean window and answers `healthy` with full confidence. Filed on 2026-08-06 off two PRs measured silent at 20:06Z; by 11:12Z on 08-07 the silence had run **17 hours** and spread to four (#1329, #1328, #1327, #1325), one of them carrying THR-1013's own fix, so the remedy for the previous class was itself trapped by this one. Diagnosis narrowed it precisely: the last `pull_request`/`push` run created anywhere was 18:04Z, while `workflow_dispatch` (20:05Z) and `schedule` (03:07Z) both ran **green**, and every silent head carried a normal `vercel` suite — so commits, webhooks, the workflow file and the runner pool were all healthy, and only the event → run-creation path was dead. Repo config ruled out (Actions `enabled`, all four workflows `state=active`). **Recovery applied before implementation**, as a technical verdict: an empty commit to each head branch created a suite within **4 seconds**, and all four PRs drained — two merged inside the hour, ending a 17-hour delivery stall. That is also the sharpest argument for the detector, since every one of those hours was pure loss against a one-line fix nobody knew to run. Fixed with a `dispatch-silence` verdict keyed on the **check-suites API** rather than the run list: an open non-draft PR whose head commit is older than `DISPATCH_SILENCE_MIN_MINUTES` (10 — measured against a 4-second healthy push and a 94-minute shortest failure, so the threshold sits in a wide empty band) and carries no `github-actions` suite. The override fires only over `healthy`/`recovered`/`transient`, the three verdicts a silenced PR falsifies; `billing-block`, `stalled` and `unknown` keep theirs, so a lesser finding never masks a more dangerous one. `standDown` stays false for the `stalled` reason — no suite means the required check never reports, the PR stays `BLOCKED`, and nothing untested reaches `main`. Unlike a stall, though, this class does **not** clear on its own, which the summary says outright and is why it is a separate verdict rather than a fold-in. 38 probe tests (+12), 960 files / 15026 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean; live end-to-end run reports `dispatch-silenced=0` post-recovery, and a live check confirms the two API shapes parse against real responses — the half pure injected tests cannot cover.

✅ **THR-781 — the event id was keyed to the agent, but the loop it was minted in iterates memberships** (2026-08-06, Social Systems Expansion) — `phaseFactionReputationDecay` walks `member_of` edges, so an agent in two factions decays in both and, on a tick where the decay crosses a rank threshold in both, pushes two demotion events under one id: `faction_decay_rank_{tick}_{agent}`, with no faction in it. React logged *"Encountered two children with the same key"*, and by its own wording one of the two demotion notices can be silently dropped — a player never told they were demoted. The multi-faction case is ordinary: `factionSeeding` mints faction nodes per chapter as `faction_def_{defId}{suffix}`, so two memberships share a `factionDefId`, hence one decay rate and demotion in lockstep. Fixed by including `edge.target`. **The guard is the deliverable** — an id collision passes every gate the repo owns (both events dispatch, both are well-formed; the only witness is a console warning nobody diffs), so the regression test builds two chapters of one guild, demotes an agent in both on one tick, and asserts two events with distinct ids and distinct `factionId`s. Falsified against the pre-fix tree, where it reports `expected 1 to be 2` on the id-set size while the *event count* passes — the shape that lets the defect hide. Sibling event-id mints in the same file swept as the ticket asked: none. 960 files / 15005 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean, 30-tick smoke at 383 agents / 47 events. Live at `?view=game&seeded&size=medium` + `__DEBUG.tick(60)`: `faction_decay_rank_60_npc_92_faction_def_builders_fellowship`, 0 console errors.

✅ **THR-927 — the gate counted claims while protecting an invariant about implementations, and hard-stopped a run over two tickets one PR was already shipping** (2026-08-03, Continuous Improvement) — `pull-work` Step 1.5 read two issues `In Dev` under the executor and exited 1 as a cross-session leak. Both were shipped by the single armed PR #1191 carrying `Fixes THR-925` and `Fixes THR-926` on their own lines, waiting only on CI; no second session existed and nothing was being built (impediment #365). Open claims and concurrent implementations are the same number only when every PR closes exactly one ticket, which the closeout protocol explicitly contradicts. Step 1.5 now resolves each claim to the open PR that closes it and counts only claims resolving to none: 0 → claim, 1 → resume, >1 → genuine leak. Two deliberate deviations from the ticket's own proposal: the keyword match is line-anchored to match `linear-autoclose.yml` exactly (THR-738), since an unanchored grep would discharge a claim on a mid-sentence mention nothing will ever close; and discharged claims never gate at any count, because the `docs-only` drain (THR-938) deliberately creates multi-PR boards that the ticket's distinct-PR formula would red-exit — including the very run that fixed it.
✅ **THR-1013 — the merge gate reported healthy for four hours while six armed PRs could not merge** (2026-08-06, Continuous Improvement) — Rule 0 pickup. From ~16:14Z GitHub accepted our jobs and gave them no machine: `Detect code changes`, normally seconds, reported as started, executed **zero steps**, and was reaped at ~15 minutes as `cancelled`, taking the required check with it. `check:actions` answered `healthy / startupFailureCount: 0` across three separate lane runs because every clause of the billing signature was absent — conclusion `cancelled` not `failure`, duration 15–31 minutes not 3–5 seconds, no annotation at all. **Cause bounded as GitHub-side**, per the ticket's first Done-when: a `workflow_dispatch` forced at 20:05Z ran the same workflow file green in 31s, so neither the file nor the runner pool was ever at fault. Fixed with a second verdict, `stalled`, keyed on the signature the first cannot see — jobs present, zero steps across all of them, past a 600s floor chosen to separate a hang from a billing failure (3–5s) and a concurrency supersede (reaped promptly). It deliberately does **not** stand the lane down: a billing block makes the gate vacuous (`skipped` satisfies branch protection) whereas `cancelled` blocks, so armed PRs merge themselves on recovery — what was missing was the sentence, not the halt. `detect` gained the `timeout-minutes` it alone lacked, commented as explicitly *not* the fix, since a timeout bounds execution and this hang was queue time. 27 probe tests (7 new on `isStalledRun`, 4 new on the classifier, including the "prefers billing-block when both classes present" precedence and a fail-soft guard against an unreadable run manufacturing an outage); 960 files / 15015 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean. Live proof on the same window that produced the false healthy: `stalledCount: 6`. Second, distinct hole found while measuring and filed rather than folded in — PRs #1327/#1328 never had a `github-actions` check suite created at all, which a run-list detector cannot see by construction (THR-1014).
✅ **THR-994 — the context strip THR-636 shipped was empty on the path players actually reach** (2026-08-06, Encounter Experience) — a THR-646 deferral. `GameView` falls back to `buildSimpleEncounterStageModel` whenever a notification's `UnifiedAction` no longer resolves, which is the common case for any encounter the player did not open mid-flight; that adapter's header carried `title` / `locationLabel: ''` / `threatLabel` / `threadTier` and **none** of `agentName`, `focalActorId`, `portraitUrl`, `reachLabel` or `hexCol`/`hexRow` — every field `ContextStrip` gates on — so THR-636's headline "whose encounter is this, and where" answer rendered as a zero-height box with no children, exactly when the player is most likely to be reading it. Fixed in the adapter alone (`GameView.tsx` untouched, which also kept it clear of THR-1005's open PR): every value comes from data the adapter already receives. **`locationLabel` returns `''` rather than the unified adapter's `'Unknown Location'`** — `ContextStrip` rejects that literal by name, so the placeholder would render as an invisible gap regardless, and the empty string is the honest form of the same outcome. Second half: resolved history rows now carry `outcome` / `outcomeWord` / `reachLabel` / `afterimage` / `replayNarrative`, so clicking a resolved step dot no longer enters replay over an empty body — the veil reads `replayNarrative || afterimage || ''`, and the rows supplied neither. No frozen `stepProseHistory` exists on this path, so replay text is the step's authored prose re-enriched under its own outcome band, the same fallback the unified adapter documents. **The tests render the real veil rather than asserting on the model**, per the Done-when, because the defect is an invisible element a shape assertion would sail past; falsified against the pre-fix tree at 7 of 8. 961 files / 15012 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean. **Browser evidence is a declared substitution:** the fallback is not reachable on demand in a seeded run — the auto-open scan surfaces encounters while their action is still live, so every naturally-opened veil takes the *unified* adapter, and the 20-tick prune window never opens before the doom clock ends the run (impediment #455). Captured instead by mounting the production `EncounterVeil` over the **live** `gameState` at 1920×1080 — real graph, real resolved action `ua_34`, real actor — showing `Vessen · Iron · Meadowcity · Show on map` with its portrait tile at `childCount: 3, height: 30px` against the ticket's measured `childCount: 0, height: 0`.

✅ **THR-1003 — the ending of an encounter did not say which encounter it was the ending of** (2026-08-06, Encounter Experience) — director review of the shipped THR-971 chip surface. The step view carries full identity chrome (encounter title, agent context strip, clickable step navigator); the aftermath carried a hand-rolled row of flat green dots in the corner reading `resolved` and nothing else — it said resolved without saying resolved *what*. Fixed by rendering the step view's header in the aftermath **from the same components, not copies**: `ContextStrip` reused unchanged, `StepNavigator` given a `mode="resolved"` reading, corner dot row deleted. Each step now shows its own outcome colour instead of one flat green for three different endings. Two decisions the reuse forced: every dot is `disabled` in resolved mode, because the aftermath path renders no replay view and a control that silently does nothing is worse than none; and the count is derived rather than asserted — `all 3 resolved` when the flow completed, `1 of 2 resolved` when it stopped early. The `AFTERMATH` marker moved below the divider into the veil's gold, since its old ghost styling now belongs to the encounter title above it. 6 new tests (title, strip contents, per-step outcome labels, early-exit count, inert navigator, marker/title distinction); 959 files / 14971 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean. Browser pass at 1920×1080 played `encounter.shrine_offering` to resolution: *Leave a Shrine Offering*, Vara / Star / Sacred Grove, three dots reading `held` / `wavered` / `held`, `all 3 resolved`, 0 new console errors. Mutex partners THR-1004 and THR-1005 remain queued and land next.

✅ **THR-1000 — a 400-seed loop was measuring a value the seed cannot move, and it only surfaced by turning someone else's PR red** (2026-08-06, Continuous Improvement) — Rule 0 pickup. `playerCastBalance.test.ts`'s `castDistribution` rebuilt a full `WorldGraph`-backed `GameState` **inside** its `SEEDS = 400` loop, and three of its five callers read only `capability` / `probability` — both computed pre-roll, before `resolveActionShared` touches the rng. So 399 of every 400 casts in those tests recomputed a constant. The 8-call inertness test sat at 113% of the 5s vitest default; PR #1313 added test weight and it failed twice in a row (5646ms → 6132ms), sole red in a 14910-test run, holding an armed auto-merge that could never fire. Fixed by hoisting the fixtures out of the loop and adding `castReadout`, a single-resolution helper for the pre-roll reads — the assertion is unchanged (same four difficulties, same two scales, same `new Set(probabilities).size === 1`), it just costs 8 casts instead of 3200. **The deliverable is the guard, not the speed-up:** the optimisation rests on a claim about where the rng enters, so `preRollStable` tracks whether any seed ever disagreed and a new test pins `castReadout` to the loop's own value — injection-proven both ways (perturbing one seed's capability reddens the stability flag; pointing the readout at the wrong cell reddens the equality and two downstream tests). Hoisting was proven behaviour-neutral by measurement rather than argument: all 7 cells return byte-identical capability, probability and outcome counts on both trees. File runs 16ms against ~7s; the target test 0ms against 5646ms. Deliberately **not** fixed by raising the timeout, per the ticket — that hides the next test to reach the cliff. 957 files / 14944 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean, 30-tick smoke at 383 agents / 47 events.

✅ **THR-769 — the four company cards have art, and the surface meant to display it turned out not to contain them** (2026-08-06, Social Systems Expansion) — a THR-732 deferral, blocked on asset authoring rather than wiring. Four plates generated and downscaled to the action-card contract (1376×768 JPEG q95, 206–270 KB, inside the 200–750 KB sibling band): *Blessing of the Bound Road*, *The Gathering Thread*, *The Unfinished Road*, *The Widening Silence*, filenames derived from `spellName` per the recipe, not from the template id. Sphere-keyed light per `SPHERE_COLORS` — violet `#cc66ff` for the three `spirit` verbs, pale teal `#8fd4c0` for `entropy`-aligned Sunder, which the card frame picks up so the mirror pair reads apart at a glance. **The registry edit cost four lines instead of eight because THR-740 merged first** — `codexRegistry.ts` imports and spreads the canonical `ACTION_ART`, so one entry reaches every surface; `actionArt.ts`'s header comment still asserted the retired second map and is corrected in the same pass. **The deliverable is the guard, not the plates.** THR-732 declined to add map entries for files that did not exist, on the sound argument that a mapped-but-missing asset renders a broken image — strictly worse than the artless fallback — but nothing enforced that the mapped paths were real, so the trade-off was resting on care alone. ✅ **THR-766 — both tunables measured and kept, and the measurement found that one of them describes a number the roll never sees** (2026-08-06, Action System & Unlocks) — THR-728's balance deferral. **God curve: keep `ASCENDANT_CAST_BASE_RAW = 6` / `ASCENDANT_CAST_AFFINITY_WEIGHT = 0.5`.** A fresh god measures capability 0.168 off-domain / 0.231 secondary / 0.354 primary, landing 64.8% success-at-cost / 28.0% clean / 4.3% near-miss / 3.0% surge at `local` over 400 seeded streams — the rulebook's texture. No template difficulty changed; the requested rarity-band sweep was run (tier 1: 104/368 in band, 258 above; tier 4: 0/5) and deliberately not acted on as cosmetics-only. 956 files / 14907 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3478, `vite build` clean, 30-tick smoke at 383 agents / 47 events.

✅ **THR-817 — the module-scope counter was fixed by deleting it, and its sweep found a feature that has never fired** (2026-08-06, Encounter Experience) — THR-816's deferral. `bandOpposition` minted band-counter action ids from a module-scope sequence, so a second same-seed run in one process continued the first run's numbering and two identical simulations serialised different ids (measured: tick 82, `ua_band_counter_11` vs `ua_band_counter_6`, every other field byte-identical); THR-816 had papered it over with a per-test `resetBandCounterIds()`. **Derived rather than relocated** — the ticket proposed moving the sequence onto `SimulationRuntime`, but a relocated counter still depends on *how many* counters were minted earlier, while `ua_band_counter_${initiatorActionId}` depends only on *what* is being answered, making uniqueness a property of construction; total because at most one counter is minted per initiator action, a counter never becomes an initiator itself, and the pool is local to one tick. ✅ **THR-972 — five director notes on the slice, and the one that looked cosmetic was hiding a determinism bug** (2026-08-02, Encounter Experience) — Christian's chat review of the test panel and nudge cards, four directives quoted verbatim into the ticket. **The motive moved from a chip below the prose to the scene's opening line above it** — it had been answering "why is this mortal here" *after* the player finished reading the scene it was meant to frame. Measured precedent: THR-792 hit this on 2026-08-02, having shipped six days earlier under THR-793's id (`15fc10f0`); that run deviated by hand and filed this ticket so the next would not have to. ✅ **THR-979 — three forks decided correctly and every authored ending was thrown away one index later** (2026-08-03, Encounter Experience) — `aftermathConfig.branchOnStep` read `1` on all three decided-fork slice templates while their forks declare `branchOnStep: 0`, so `resolveAftermathVariant` looked for a choice at a step none is ever written to and returned `fallback` on every resolution. **The noun was verified before the verb** (CLAUDE.md protocol, and the ticket asked for it explicitly): a CLI run of the real template returned `choiceHistory: [{ stepIndex: 0, choiceId: 'negative', interventionType: 'agent_decided' }]`, which settled the ticket's open question — the fork records fine, the aftermath reads the wrong index — and pointed the fix at content rather than at `branchDecision.ts`. **The trap is that the two `branchOnStep` fields are the same quantity with identical JSDoc**, but a fork sits one slot *after* the step it decides on, so writing the fork's own position type-checks perfectly and kills all six endings silently, taking the Full Moon Collection seed with it. **The test that should have caught it was the reason it shipped:** THR-971's adapter test hand-built `choiceHistory` at `stepIndex: 1` to match the buggy config — inventing both sides of the comparison — so it agreed with itself and went green; it is now bound to the *fork's* declared index, which is the direction that can still fail. **The invariant needed widening as well as writing.** A first pass hooked into `assertValidUnifiedTemplate` and was **vacuous** — falsified by reverting a template and watching the suite stay green, because that helper is wired to only three content sets and the slice is in none of them — so the guard is exported and swept over the whole catalog, with a non-empty-population assertion so it cannot quietly go vacuous again. Scoped deliberately to `decidedBy` forks: the audit surfaced a second class of 13 templates carrying variants with **no fork at all**, dead for the unrelated reason that the player-pick path was retired, filed as THR-989 rather than folded in. Verified in the live sim after the fix — the crossroads now resolves "The bargain is struck…" where it previously returned the fallback prose the ticket quoted. 951 files / 14811 tests, ratchet unchanged at 3478, build green, 30-tick smoke at 383 agents.
✅ **THR-957 — the kill criteria that would retire intent-judge were unfalsifiable, and half of them still are** (2026-08-03, Continuous Improvement) — `intent-judge` § Metrics to track claimed "`retrospective` skill consumes Fridays"; that skill contained no reference to `Docs/judge-metrics/` and never had, so the weekly aggregation had never run in the 11 weeks rows were being written. Wired as `retrospective` § Step 5c per the ticket's recommended option (a). **The consumer had to read by header name, not column index** — six files carry **four different table shapes** (two with an extra `Linear` column; `2026-W29.md` in lowercase kebab with `impact-class` *before* `verdict`), and the positional first pass returned `THR-75`, `THR-457` and `High-risk` as verdicts: plausible-looking output, entirely wrong, and nothing would have flagged it. Glob is loose (`YYYY-W?ww`) so the two pre-convention filenames are not silently dropped, which the ticket had flagged. **The finding the ticket did not anticipate is that option (a) is only half-available.** Two of the four Kill criteria are keyed on *user overrides* and no column records one, so they cannot be computed no matter how many weeks accumulate — and a consumer reporting `0% override rate` would have laundered an unmeasured criterion into a **passing** one, which is strictly worse than the gap it replaced. They are reported `NOT MEASURABLE (no override column)`, and an optional `Overridden` column now exists so they become computable prospectively; historical rows are left un-backfilled because no honest value exists for them. Kill criteria are now a table carrying a "measurable today?" column, so the distinction cannot be lost again. **Dry run (Done-when 3), 11 rows over 2026-05-15 → 2026-07-30:** Allow 81.8% (9/11), escalation 0.0%, median latency 92.5s (n=10, one row unparseable), override rate not measurable — **no criterion met, keep the skill**, with the caveat stated in place that 11 rows is below the "full month" every criterion requires, so the numbers are directional rather than a verdict. The 0.0% escalation rate sits under intent-judge's own declared floor of 0.05 and is recorded as a tuning signal, not a retirement one.

✅ **THR-978 — the field THR-971's taxonomy named as the toll source contains no words, so the shipped mapping was right and the deviation note was wrong** (2026-08-03, Encounter Experience) — decided Option B and closed. `QuintessenceEvent` carries `targetNodeId`, `delta`, `source`, `tick`, and none of the four is authored prose: `delta` is a magnitude the nudge-model surface rules forbid rendering (its own type header says the same — "Displayed prose-only via IPK — never show numbers to player"), `source` is a machine token whose chip would be a key:value label rather than a sentence, and the other two say nothing about a price. The decisive argument is not that it is awkward to render but that it is **redundant**: `computeOutcomeConsequence` derives the event purely from the outcome band — reward on `critical_success`, penalty on `success_at_cost` and `critical_failure`, `null` on the remaining three — and the ending already carries that band in `EncounterAftermathSummary.outcome` / `narrativeTag`, so the only thing the Q event adds over what the chip can already see is the magnitude, which is exactly the part that may not be shown. Surfacing it would therefore require authoring a new (band × source) → sentence table, i.e. **a second vocabulary** — the one thing `buildAftermathConsequences.ts`'s own header forbids ("a re-presentation, never a second vocabulary") — and on a `success_at_cost` ending it would double-report a price the authored change set has already stated in words. Option A is not deferred; it is ruled out, and the header now records that as a design rule with its reasoning in place of the "tracked separately" deviation note. **Written at both ends deliberately:** the ticket was itself discovered by grepping `quintessenceEvent` from the engine side, so `OutcomeConsequence.quintessenceEvent` is marked engine-internal with a pointer to the adapter, closing the loop for the next grep-driven reader rather than only for someone already working on chips. Comment-only, zero runtime effect; full code gate run anyway because the diff contains `.ts` paths (949 files / 14803 tests, ratchet unchanged at 3478, build green, 30-tick engine smoke at 383 agents).

✅ **THR-946 — the merge queue's agent half landed inert, and the click it was waiting for never came** (2026-08-02, Continuous Improvement) — archived from `project-status.md` because its premise died four days later. ✅ **THR-930 — the armed-PR probe filtered its own input on arming, so an unarmed conflicted PR was invisible rather than misclassified** (2026-08-02, Continuous Improvement) — `listArmedPrs` ended with `all.filter(pr => pr.autoMergeRequest !== null)`, which made arming a condition of *entry* to the health check rather than a property of a PR inside it. THR-897 had fixed classification within that set (`DIRTY` distinguished from `BEHIND`); this is the ring outside it, and the failure mode is strictly worse than misclassification because there is nothing in the output to be suspicious of. Reproduced first-hand at claim time rather than taken from the ticket: this run's own pull-work Step 0.8 emitted `{"verdict":"healthy","summary":"No PRs are waiting to merge.","counts":{"drainable":0,"conflicted":0,...}}`, and `gh pr list --state open` seconds later on the same tree returned exactly one PR — #1114, `DIRTY`, `autoMergeRequest: null`, open since 2026-07-30T12:21Z — with THR-860 holding an In-Dev slot for the whole 77 hours. Membership is now **open and non-draft**, and `armed` becomes a per-PR field (`armedCount` / `unarmedCount` at the top level) so the split stays legible to the two consuming lanes. **Drafts remain excluded deliberately:** a draft is the one case where "not trying to merge yet" is an author's explicit signal rather than an inference from a missing flag, so widening past it would start reporting work nobody claimed was finished. **Widening the set forced two secondary decisions, either of which would have replaced the old wrong answer with a new one.** First, `updateCandidate` is now filtered on `klass === "drainable" && armed`: `gh pr update-branch` on an unarmed PR refreshes a branch that auto-merge will never act on, so naming one would be a no-op reported as progress — the `drainable` summary gained a second arm for that case rather than printing `oldest first (#null)`. Second, the staleness clock changed source. `enabledAtMs` came from `autoMergeRequest.enabledAt` with `|| Date.now()` behind it, and an unarmed PR has no `enabledAt` — so every unarmed PR would have measured **zero minutes old on every single run**, a conflicted PR reporting as brand new forever, which is the identical silence being fixed one layer down. Renamed `clockStartMs` (arming when armed, `createdAt` when not) specifically so the two events cannot be treated as interchangeable by the next reader. **Unarmed conflicts run their own slower tiers** — `UNARMED_DIRTY_ESCALATE_HOURS` 6 and `UNARMED_DIRTY_ABANDONED_HOURS` 24, against 90 minutes and 12 hours armed — because arming is a promise to merge *now* and its absence justifies patience, not silence; a test pins that a 13-hour conflict is `abandoned` when armed and merely `conflicted` when not, so the distinction is behavioural rather than decorative. Verified against the real defect rather than a fixture: the widened probe reports `verdict: "abandoned"`, `needsChristian: true`, `updateCandidate: null`, `conflictFiles: ["Docs/project-status.md"]` for #1114. Ten new tests (27 → 37). The file, npm script, and exported symbols keep their `armed` names — renaming would ripple through `package.json`, two skill docs and a plan doc for no behavioural gain, and the decision is recorded in the header so it reads as a choice rather than an oversight.

✅ **THR-828 — `check:process` printed "passed" for a run whose three Linear-backed assertions never executed** (2026-08-02, Continuous Improvement) — with `LINEAR_API_KEY` unset the lint skipped recent plan references, orphan issues, and Ready-for-Dev handoff keywords, recorded one warning, and closed with `check:process passed with 1 warning(s).` A scheduled lane legitimately runs without the credential, so the defect was never the skip — it was the verdict: the output asserted a pass for coverage it did not have, which is worse than an unread advisory gate because a reader who greps `check:process passed` gets a true string and a false impression. The handoff-keyword check is the one that stings, being exactly what would have caught the missing-coordination-block failure mode that left a promoted issue at the top of the queue being refused by `pull-work` Step 3 every hour. Shipped the ticket's preferred shape (option 1): a three-state verdict `passed` / `passed-with-gaps` / `failed`, where any skipped sub-check forces the middle state and the summary names what did not run and why. **Exit-code semantics are unchanged by design** — `passed-with-gaps` still exits 0 — because the goal is an honest report, not a lane that stops working without credentials. **Skipped sub-checks are registered in their own list rather than as warning findings:** a skip is the absence of a finding, and conflating the two is the mechanism by which three un-executed assertions were counted as one warning and waved through. **The predicate covers four skip sites, not the one the title names** — the unset key, each of the two Linear GraphQL fetches failing independently, and the `npm_execpath`-gated nested plan-doc lint — which is what makes the summary track real coverage instead of restating a constant; demonstrated by the delta across three live runs (4 skips bare, 4 with distinct `HTTP 401` fetch-failure reasons under a bogus key, 3 under `npm` where the plan-doc lint genuinely ran). **A second-order defect surfaced in the same read and is fixed here rather than filed:** the plan-reference fallback emitted a hard **error** when no matching issue was found, but a failed fetch leaves `recentIssueNodes` empty and is indistinguishable from a successful empty search — so a network blip manufactured an error against every plan file lacking an inline Linear link. It is now gated on the fetch having actually returned, which is the same thesis as the headline fix (a check that did not run must not report a verdict). Verdict logic lives in `scripts/process-check-verdict.ts` because `check-process.ts` runs `void main()` at module scope and cannot be imported by a test — the reason `coordination-block-predicate.ts` already sits beside it — and its 16 cases pin both arms: the uncovered run away from the exact string the old code emitted, and the covered run *to* the bare `passed` form, since a formatter that always says `passed-with-gaps` trains its reader to ignore the token just as effectively. **The covered-Linear arm is proven by unit test rather than a live run and this is stated rather than implied:** no `LINEAR_API_KEY` exists in the automation sandbox. The ticket's "adjacent" note — two `check:canon-staleness` warnings that can never be cleared because they demand `last_reviewed` frontmatter on generated artifacts — was deliberately not folded in, per its own instruction.

✅ **THR-756 — the drift scan deduped on a title containing the run date, so it filed a fresh duplicate of every unchanged signal every week** (2026-08-02, Continuous Improvement) — the weekly scan opens one Linear issue per red signal and guarded against duplicates with `findIssueByExactTitle`, but its own title format embeds the run date (`Drift scan [<runDate>]: <signal> — <summary>`), which makes exact-title comparison false even when the drift is byte-identical. The 07-22 and 07-24 runs alone produced five duplicate pairs (THR-706↔THR-746 UL drift, THR-707↔THR-747 skill freshness, THR-708↔THR-748 rulebook→UL, THR-709↔THR-749 IMPL tags, THR-710↔THR-750 quick-ref vs rulebook) — every run doubling the open count for the same underlying drift, with a groomer hand-deduping after. Dedup is now scoped to the **signal** rather than the exact title: one query per run fetches the open `drift-scan` issues, `driftIssueSignalName` recovers the signal from a position-anchored parse of the title, and an existing match is refreshed in place — title and description updated to the current run, plus a comment preserving the previous title so the week-over-week movement in a signal's counts survives the description overwrite (NFP #2). **The matcher is deliberately not a substring test.** The Linear query filters on the `drift-scan` label alone, so the matcher is the only thing standing between the scan and adopting — then overwriting — the wrong issue: a `coupling creep` issue whose summary happens to mention UL drift, or a human-filed ticket named "Rework the UL drift signal thresholds", would both match a naive `includes`, and those are the cases the new tests discriminate rather than the easy negatives that any implementation passes. **Openness is asserted three ways** (state type `nin` completed/canceled, plus null `completedAt` *and* null `canceledAt`) because the five duplicates sit in Linear's **Duplicate** state, which surfaces as its own status while populating `canceledAt`; testing the timestamps makes the exclusion independent of how a terminal state is typed, and refreshing a closed duplicate instead of filing would be a strictly worse failure than the one being fixed. **The GraphQL filter shape is the one surface no test reaches** — `LINEAR_API_KEY` is unset in the sandbox, so it is unvalidated against the live schema — which is exactly why the lookup is wrapped in a fail-soft that falls back to the pre-fix exact-title path: a rejected filter costs one warning and the old duplicate-filing behaviour, never a dead scan. The second Done-when required no work: the 2026-07-25 grooming run had already closed the five 07-22 issues with `duplicateOf` relations. The cadence proof ("two consecutive runs with unchanged drift produce one issue, not two") accrues on the next scheduled Friday scan and is not claimed here.

✅ **THR-971 — the ending never admitted what it planted, and the screen meant to say so could not render at all** (2026-08-02, Encounter Experience) — Christian, slice review: *"all the stuff in the original prototype we made is not there."* The aftermath drew generic actor-moments/highlights/changes inherited from the pre-nudge modal, so the slice's genuine `encounter_seed` plantings — the crossroads plants The Full Moon Collection ~132 ticks out — were never mentioned; the world changed invisibly, THR-907 verdict 3 failing at the UI layer rather than the sim layer. Shipped `buildAftermathConsequences.ts`: a pure, React-free mapping from the **existing** engine vocabulary onto the mockup's five chips (prize / standing / toll / wound / seed) plus a `mark` fail-soft bucket, so an unrecognised change kind still renders — a consequence the screen does not admit is the exact defect the taxonomy exists to kill. Seeds are read from the resolved variant's reaction effects rather than re-authored, so an author cannot state a planting twice or forget to. Chips render as toned hairlines, not boxed cards, keeping the veil's dissolved-into-void aesthetic; named entities inside a chip resolve through a new optional `entityId` threaded from the narrative linker and are clickable **only** where a node actually resolved and a handler is wired — fail-open, never a dead link. **The second defect was found by trying to verify the first, and was the more serious of the two:** `EncounterVeil` memoised `narratableProse` *after* its aftermath early return, so the instant a mounted veil crossed from encounter into aftermath React counted one hook fewer and threw `Rendered fewer hooks than expected`, taking the whole ending to the error boundary. That is the ordinary play path — resolve an encounter, watch it end — and it **predates this ticket** (HEAD carries the identical early-return-before-`useMemo` structure; this diff adds zero hooks), which means the surface being redesigned could not render in the live app at all. Hoisted above every early return and pinned by a transition regression test that rerenders a mounted veil into aftermath. **Two of the ticket's stated sources turned out unreachable and the deviations are documented rather than papered over:** `toll` cannot read `consequence.quintessenceEvent` — it lives on `OutcomeConsequence`, is consumed per-step by the pending-quintessence queue, and is never persisted onto `UnifiedAction` (THR-978) — so it reads the authored change set's losses, which is where an encounter states its price in words anyway; and the approved mockup all three sibling tickets measure against exists on no branch, in no history (THR-980). Done-when proven against real shipped content rather than fixtures: the accept ending yields exactly one SEED chip naming the Full Moon follow-up, and the refuse ending — same template, same adapter, same code path — yields none. **Filed rather than folded in (THR-979):** driven live, the crossroads resolved to `fallback` both times, so the authored variants may be unreachable in play and the seed never actually planted; the chip surface correctly showed no seed chip for that plants-nothing ending, which is the falsification case working as designed.

✅ **THR-970 — a model field added "for the pip row" had no renderer, and the seam was invisible because both sides shipped green** (2026-08-02, Encounter Experience) — THR-892 added `EncounterStageFactorLineModel.delta` with a doc comment naming its purpose (signed 0–1, "for the pip row", absent ⇒ draw nothing) and THR-890 rendered pips on cards and forecast but never on factor lines; the handoff sentence "the model carries the number, THR-890 renders it" was the entire specification and nothing tested the join, so both closed green with the feature unbuilt. Shipped the missing `OddsPips` row in `NudgePhaseShell` behind named size/gap constants (NFP #1), guarded by a render test asserting **both** arms of the contract plus a third case pinning which lines populate each arm, so a future adapter change dropping every delta cannot leave the suite vacuously passing. ✅ **THR-946 — the merge queue's agent half, landed deliberately inert so the settings click cannot arrive first** (2026-08-02, Continuous Improvement) — THR-735 decided GitHub's merge queue as the structural fix for the `BEHIND` livelock (an armed green PR knocked stale by an unrelated merge never merges on its own, and Step 0.8's sweep can drain at most one per advance of `main`'s tip — the defect is serialization, not throughput). This ticket is the execution of that decision, not a re-argument of it. **`merge_group: types: [checks_requested]` added to `ci.yml`, which is a prerequisite rather than an enhancement:** without the trigger the required checks never report on a merge group and *every* queued PR stalls until timeout, so the plan's own fail-soft table requires the trigger to land before the click. Both required checks — `Test · Typecheck · Build` and `Docs gates` — hang off this one workflow, so one trigger covers the two overlapping protection surfaces THR-735 found disagreeing on `main`. **`dorny/paths-filter` cannot classify this event** — it derives its diff base from the push/pull_request payload, which `merge_group` does not carry — so both filter steps now sit the event out and a third producer computes `code`/`docs` from `git diff --name-only <base_sha> HEAD`. **The docs-only skip is preserved inside the queue, as a deliberate decision with its reasoning recorded:** always running the suite is simpler, but it would put every hourly briefing and orchestrator sweep through the ~10.5-minute gate and batch them behind each other — the same lane congestion the queue is adopted to remove; free public runners make this a latency argument, not a cost one. **That is only safe if `skipped` can never mean "unclassified", so THR-768's vacuous-gate reasoning was re-derived for the event rather than assumed to carry over:** every failure mode in the new step — unresolvable `base_sha`, `git diff` error, malformed pattern — exits non-zero under `set -euo pipefail`, which fails `detect`, which the existing guard converts into a **failing** required check. There is no path on which a change goes unclassified and is waved through. **Two GitHub-expression traps were caught in design, both silent and both surfacing only after the queue is live:** `A && 0 || 1` evaluates to `1` on *both* branches because the number `0` is falsy and loses the `||`, so the conditional `fetch-depth` uses quoted `'0'`/`'1'`; and the output fallback `steps.filter.outputs.code || steps.filter-merge-group.outputs.code` is correct *precisely because* a skipped step yields `''` (the only falsy string) while a genuine `'false'` is non-empty and therefore truthy — the asymmetry is load-bearing and is commented so a future reader does not "fix" it. **The predicate is now written three times, so it is pinned twice over:** `scripts/__tests__/docs-code-decoupling.test.ts` checks the pattern structurally against `DOC_EXCLUDED_GLOBS` + `DOC_TO_CODE_ALLOWLIST`, *executes* it as a `RegExp` against doc and code fixtures (including a `src/data/*.generated.json` near-miss proving the exclusions stay exact paths rather than globs), and cross-checks it against `isDocPath`. Falsified in two arms before shipping — dropping the `ul-dashboard` exclusion reddens 2 tests, removing the trigger reddens 1. **Done-whens 2 and 3 are strictly post-click and are not claimed:** a real code PR and a real docs PR landing through the queue, and `linear-autoclose` firing on a queue-produced merge — the latter expected sound by inspection (it triggers on `pull_request: [closed]` and on `push` to `main`, both of which a queue merge produces), which is exactly what a live Done-when exists to convert into a measurement. **THR-945's script is retired by never having been written** — no disturber-pays script exists in `scripts/` (the only armed-PR tooling is `check-armed-prs.ts`, THR-702/THR-897's classifier, which stays), and THR-947 removed the exhaust that was its whole premise. Mutex with THR-939 reversed on evidence: `Done`, merged as PR #1243. Lane docs updated in `pull-work` (Step 0.8 + closeout, with a one-line queue-liveness probe so a session cannot mistake the trigger's presence for the queue being on) and CLAUDE.md's Definition of Done.

✅ **THR-347 — a constants-tuning playtest found its own premise dead: the pipeline consuming four of five constant families has no producer** (2026-08-02, Encounter Experience) — the ticket asked to calibrate `src/data/encounter-experience-constants.ts` against play data. Measured first, at `--seed 42 --map medium`, 383 agents, 120 ticks: `pendingChoiceCommits` `[]`, `regionalDetectionPressure` `[]`, zero threshold crossings of any band. **Nothing in production enqueues a `PendingChoiceCommit`** — every non-test reference is a read or a clear, and `effectiveProbability` has no writer — so `phaseChoiceResolution` early-returns every tick and `CHOICE_PROBABILITY_TILT_*` / `CHOICE_DRIFT_MAGNITUDE_*` / `DETECTION_THRESHOLD_*` are test-only reachable (THR-964). `CHOICE_PROBABILITY_TILT_*` would be inert even with a producer: it is computed solely to fill a trace field, and `resolveEncounterChoice` takes `effectiveProbability` as given. Two defects fell out: detection pressure is fed **essence costs (1/2/3) into a 0–1 clamped scale**, so the smallest delta is 0.8 and the three-band rival ladder fires all at once (THR-963); and the live drift writer is `branchDecision` using `BRANCH_DECISION_DRIFT_MAGNITUDE = 0.08` from a *different file*, whose comment promises "three in the same direction register" against `DRIFT_THRESHOLD_SOFT = 0.30` when `3 × 0.08 = 0.24` (THR-965). **No constant was changed** — the honest deliverable was the measurement and three follow-ups, not a plausible diff with no player-visible effect.

✅ **THR-806 — sixteen glossary terms were defined but unfindable, and the two that looked most missing were actually dead links** (2026-08-02, Content Architecture) — `Docs/ubiquitous-language/README.md` is the **always-load** UL footprint (CLAUDE.md loads it every session; shards load on demand), so a term present in a shard but absent from that index is invisible to any session that does not already know to open the shard — exactly the failure the UL exists to prevent, a session minting a rival term for a concept already defined. **Re-measured at pickup rather than inherited, and the ticket's numbers had already rotted:** it reported 110 shard terms / 96 indexed; the tree held **118 / 102**, and the README footer itself claimed both "118 canonical terms" and "102 of the 116", flagging its own inconsistency in prose. The drift accumulated across three separate waves — the nine mentorship terms in Agents (THR-782 era), the four scene-cast terms in Encounters (THR-696), one straggler (`Domain Canon Page`) in Process. **Two of the sixteen were a different defect, and the ticket's own prescription would have made them worse.** The Graph versioning pair *was* indexed — under hand-typed anchors `./Graph.md#worldversion--touchworld` and `#structuralcacheversion--touchstructure`, with a double hyphen no heading can slugify to, since `slugifyHeading` collapses `-+` → `-`. Both links were dead. "Add an index bullet for each of the 16 missing terms" would have appended duplicates beside two corpses rather than repairing them; they were repaired. This is the precise hazard the ticket warned about in the abstract ("anchors must match `slugifyHeading` output rather than hand-typed guesses") occurring in its own measurement. **The diff was run in both directions for that reason** — term→index catches absence, index→term catches dangling — and both now report zero, at 118 of 118. **Why three waves passed unnoticed is the durable finding.** `scripts/generate-ul-dashboard-data.ts` parses *both* files and emits a `missing_one_liner` warning, so it looks like the guard already exists — but it **falls back to each term's first body sentence** when the README has no entry, so `?view=ul` renders a sensible summary for all 118 and warns on **none** of the drifted 16 (measured warning set: 7 × `unresolved_see_also`, unchanged before and after this change). The warning is about *summary quality*; this is about *index membership*; the fallback makes the second condition unobservable by construction. The footer now carries the invariant, the verification recipe, and that trap stated explicitly, so the next reader can check it rather than trusting a count. **The guard was decided, not skipped:** THR-806's scope item 2 asked whether it earns a blocking gate — it does, and it is filed as **THR-959** (both directions, reusing the generator's exported `slugifyHeading`, wired into the `Docs gates` job) rather than built in-run, because a `scripts/` change would have flipped this `docs-only` ticket onto the code track mid-drain and ended it. Docs-only diff (THR-917 classification empty); `check:generated-freshness`, `lint:plan-doc` and `check:impediment-ids` green.

✅ **THR-762 — a skill told its subagent to do the one thing its own hard rule forbade, and the resulting silence lasted the skill's entire life** (2026-08-02, Continuous Improvement) — `.claude/skills/intent-judge/SKILL.md` Procedure step 8 instructed the judge to append a metrics row to `Docs/judge-metrics/YYYY-WW.md`; its Hard rules said "**Never edits any file**". ✅ **THR-947 — The coordination layer stored its state on protected `main`, so the paperwork competed with the product** (2026-08-02, Continuous Improvement) — implementing Christian's chat verdict that the building documents "are just scaffolding". Every hourly status artifact reached `main` by branch → PR → CI → merge, and under strict branch protection each such merge knocks every in-flight PR to `BEHIND` at ~18 minutes a re-run; measured 2026-08-01 10:24–14:24Z, **8 merges to `main` and only 3 of them product code**. Exhaust — `Design/briefing.md`, `Design/user-actions.md`, and the orchestrator / backlog-grooming / weekly-hygiene / test-suite-health run reports — now publishes to an unprotected **`ops` branch**: no PR, no CI, no auto-merge, and `main`'s tip does not move. One shared entry point, `scripts/ops-publish.sh`, commits via git **plumbing** (`hash-object` / `update-index` / `commit-tree`) against a throwaway index and pushes directly. **Plumbing rather than a checkout is what makes it safe for these particular lanes:** it touches no working tree, so the THR-672 home-tree rule holds by construction; it creates no worktree, so the THR-797 reaped-worktree-retargets-git trap cannot fire; and it leaves the caller's branch, index and HEAD untouched, so a lane can publish mid-session. **The half the ticket did not name was the read side, and both of its failures are silent.** Four surfaces resolved sibling reports by listing the local `Docs/ops/`, which after the cutover holds only the frozen pre-cutover archive: `keep-work-flowing-cc` step 2.6 would have folded months-old `## Needs Christian` items into the brief while passing every freshness check on filename alone, and the orchestrator's run-letter picker would have reported "no runs today" so every run of the day reused the same filename — on a branch where a push is last-writer-wins, losing reports outright rather than conflicting visibly. All four read `origin/ops` now, with the fallback to the local directory explicitly forbidden. **`check:substantive` had the mirror-image defect:** its briefing baseline was hardcoded to `origin/main`, where the file is now a pointer stub, so it would have compared every real brief against the stub, never matched, and returned `commit` on every run — silently un-doing THR-920, the gate that exists to stop exactly that. The ref follows the file (`DEFAULT_BASELINE_REF`, overridable via `--baseline-ref`), **verified in both directions rather than assumed**: the live brief against `origin/ops` returns `skip` / `digest-unchanged` / `baselineFound: true`, and a missing ref fails soft to `commit`. **History stays on `main`, frozen** — a dated archive cannot be mistaken for a current copy, so only the two always-current `Design/` files needed pointer stubs. Membership is a **predicate**, not a list (THR-688 rule A, written up in the new `Docs/ops/README.md`), so a future lane's report is a member the day it is written; the registry, the prompt mirrors, the containment-script mirrors, the dated one-off forensics and the gated impediment dashboard were each excluded with their reason. Both live scheduled-task prompts and their four `Docs/ops/scheduled-task-prompts/` mirrors updated in the same pass and verified byte-identical. Full suite green at 937 files / 14592 tests; typecheck ratchet unchanged at 3481. Done-whens 2/4/5 are multi-hour observation windows and remain open by construction; the substantive-change gate's now-dead premise is filed as THR-954 rather than settled in-run. `Browser-verify exempt: process/infrastructure change, no UI surface`.

✅ **THR-940 — The test suite spent more time importing modules than running tests, and the fix had to be split three ways rather than two** (2026-08-01, Continuous Improvement) — vitest ran each of 936 files in its own isolated worker, re-importing the heavy engine/data module graph every time: a full run reported `import 573.68s` against `tests 341.45s`, so most of the cost was per-file overhead, not testing. The suite now runs as **three projects under one `vitest run`** — `node` (807 files, `pool: 'threads'`, `isolate: false`), `node-isolated` (21), `dom` (109) — with `npm test` unchanged, which is load-bearing because the CI job name `Test · Typecheck · Build` is a **required** status check that must not move. **The ticket specified two pools and two is not enough:** files using `vi.mock` cannot share a worker either, because a shared module registry defeats module mocking — whichever file imports the real module first wins. That failure is *worse than a crash*: in `grantedTraitConsumers.test.ts` it made one assertion **pass for the wrong reason** (the unmocked lookup returned undefined, so the template carried no `requiredTraits` and sailed through the very gate it was meant to be blocked by) while two others failed. Four engine files that fail under shared workers and pass alone are **pinned with their reason and a Deferral (THR-949)** rather than quietly opted out: three carry module-scope state across file boundaries (the hazard CLAUDE.md names under *Load-Bearing Architectural Decisions*), the fourth asserts a 500ms wall-clock budget that shared-worker allocation pressure pushes over. **Two of the four were invisible locally and surfaced only on CI's first run**, which is the durable finding: under `isolate: false` the grouping of files into workers depends on worker count *and* on the order files finish, so a green run on a 32-core box does not prove the pin list complete — the limitation, and the constrained-run recipe for hunting the next one, are recorded in the partition module. Guarded by 8 tests carrying population floors (≥50 dom, ≥10 mockers, ≥500 suite) plus a ≥75% floor on the shared pool, so neither an empty scan nor a creeping re-isolation can go vacuously green. Full suite green at 937 files / 14592 tests; typecheck ratchet unchanged at 3481.

✅ **THR-941 — The hex map documented as deleted three phases ago was still in the tree, and still being tested** (2026-08-01, Continuous Improvement) — CLAUDE.md's Rejected Approaches list has claimed since Phase 8 that the V1 SVG hex map was deleted, and `08-VERIFICATION.md` recorded it "✓ VERIFIED — not tracked by git at HEAD"; `src/components/HexMap/` was nonetheless present with 19 files (11 components/hooks, 8 tests, 2,678 lines), so CI tested dead code on every full run while the documentation everyone reads said it was gone. **The ticket's own predicate was re-run at pickup rather than trusted, and the snapshot had already rotted** — it said 9 component files, the tree held 11. **Deadness established four ways, because one static-import grep is exactly how a lazily-imported module survives a dead-code sweep:** no `components/HexMap[^V]` hit in `src/` or `index.html`, no relative import into the tree from outside, no dynamic `import()`, no reference from `vite.config.ts` / `index.html` / `wiki-manifest.json` / `scripts/`; the only name collision (`shouldRenderIndividualOnHexMap`) is an unrelated function in a Game test. **No live behaviour lost its only test** — the 8 deleted tests cover only the deleted components, and the shared modules they touched keep independent coverage (`engine/coastline` ×2, `hexMath` ×3, HexMapV2 ×41). **The typecheck ratchet corroborated the blast radius numerically instead of merely passing:** the total fell by exactly 11, matching the sum of the 7 baseline entries for the deleted files, proving the deletion removed those errors and nothing else; baseline refreshed to 3481 to hold the new floor. ✅ **THR-939 — The post-merge full-suite re-run is gone, and the reason it had to go is not the reason on the ticket** (2026-08-01, Continuous Improvement) — under **strict** branch protection a branch must be up to date with `main` before it merges, so the tree landing on `main` is byte-identical to the one `Test · Typecheck · Build` validated on `pull_request` minutes earlier; the push-to-`main` run re-derived a known answer 38 times in two weeks. **The stated justification was void before pickup and is rewritten rather than inherited:** it costed those runs at ~22% of the CI bill, but THR-919's audit established the repo is **public** on `ubuntu-latest` standard runners, which GitHub bills at **$0** — there is no spend to cut. Mutex on THR-909 cleared before landing (Done, PR #1210 merged). Residual named, not silently left: `Docs gates` still runs on a docs-merge push, ~2 min of the same redundancy.

✅ **THR-938 — Paperwork stopped consuming code slots, and the fix had to defuse the WIP gate to be safe** (2026-08-01, Continuous Improvement) — roughly a dozen of ~60 Ready-for-Dev tickets are docs/process-only, and one-issue-per-run made each burn a whole hourly slot, so source-code work queued behind CLAUDE.md corrections and UL proposals. Queue retro-tagged to 15 `docs-only` (6 verified by full Done-when read, 8 by unambiguous named surface); THR-839 and THR-756 rejected as code-track on `scripts/impediment-log.ts` and `scripts/drift-scan/index.ts`. ✅ **THR-735 — The armed-PR stall got its verdict, and the deciding fact was that `main` is protected twice** (2026-08-01, Continuous Improvement) — six occurrences over nine days of armed green PRs idling at `BEHIND` while reading healthy. ✅ **THR-872 — Four producers wrote it, nothing read it, and every First was described in the same default words** (2026-07-31, Content Architecture) — `MeetingEncounterResult.traitSeeds` had four authoring sources — legacy dilemmas, the 167-template enriched library, spark visions, and THR-868's bond reception — and `createAgentFromMeeting` never read the field, so **366 distinct authored descriptors were discarded at the graph boundary**. The test enumerates the population from all four catalogs with **each source asserted non-empty individually**, because a combined check would pass with three of the four dead — the vacuous-probe shape this ticket's own Done-when named.

✅ **THR-916 — A generated file was also a tracked file, so every merge re-conflicted every other open PR** (2026-08-01, Continuous Improvement) — `Design/impediment-dashboard.html` is ~6,400 lines of which ~6,200 are rendered from `Docs/impediments.md`, and it was **committed**.
