The part that churns is no longer in the tree; the part in the tree no longer churns. **The consumer audit cleared approach 1 on evidence, not assumption** — the render is absent from `public/wiki-manifest.json`, lives outside `public/` so Vite never serves it, is imported by no `src/` file, and falls outside `vercel.json`'s `ignoreCommand` inputs, so nothing reads it from git; `Design/*` was *already* gitignored and the file was tracked only because impediment #139 force-added it. **Losslessness was proven, not asserted:** deleting the render and regenerating from the committed template alone — simulating a fresh clone — reproduces the previously committed 6,423 lines **byte-identical**. **Untracking did not buy coverage from the gate,** which the ticket's Done-when named explicitly: `check:generated-freshness` gains an `UNCOMMITTED_GENERATED_PATHS` branch asking the two questions that still have teeth — does the generator still produce it, and is it still untracked — the second being the load-bearing one, since it catches the `git add -f` that started this. `replaceGeneratedBlock` now **throws** on missing markers instead of returning its input unchanged: silence was survivable in the in-place design (the file kept its old data and merely went stale) and is fatal when rendering from a template, where it would ship a dashboard reporting **zero impediments** — indistinguishable from a healthy log. **Falsified rather than asserted:** force-adding the render fails exactly one of the six new pins (`expected true to be false`) and no others. **Only the dashboard half of impediment #358 is claimed** — the duplicate-number half is unchanged and remains covered by `check:impediment-ids` (THR-881), which fails the losing lane's PR before its merge lands because strict protection forces the branch up to date first, with the residue that on a docs-only PR that gate runs in the not-yet-required `Docs gates` job (THR-931). Full suite green (944 files, 14,623 tests); typecheck ratchet 3492 unchanged; `vite build` clean; `check:generated-freshness` and `check:wiki-freshness:blocking` pass.

✅ **THR-919 — CI costs $0, and the lever ranked most confident was the only one that would start a bill** (2026-08-01, Continuous Improvement) — the ticket asked to cut CI wall time against a reported ~$50/month, and its coordination block said to start with the cost caveat rather than the code. That was right: the premise did not survive one query. **`christianspliid-ui/threadbare` is public and every workflow runs on `ubuntu-latest`**, so Actions bills it **nothing** — standard runners are free on public repositories. The ticket's own reconstruction (~1,150 min/month × $0.008 ≈ $9/month) had assumed a *private* repo, so neither the $50 nor the $9 was ever the number. **The unreadable billing API stopped being a blocker rather than being worked around**: it existed only to test "is the $50 this suite", and repo visibility answers that without it, since a free service cannot be $50 of anything. **The lever ranking inverts at its top entry** — a larger runner was framed as "bills 2×/min, spend is flat", but GitHub charges larger runners **even on public repos**, making lever 1 the only one that *creates* cost where none exists and therefore a Christian-owned spend decision, not an engineering one; sharding becomes the strongest free wall-clock lever, gated on the fact that `Test · Typecheck · Build` is a **required** check and a matrix must land a same-named aggregator in the same PR or `main` stops being mergeable. **A third finding governs how any successor may measure itself:** five consecutive executed jobs on 2026-08-01 ran `Run tests` at 426/427/745/948/913s — a **2.2× spread with the suite unchanged** — so the 889s in the description is one sample from a noisy distribution, this ticket's Done-when #1 (single before/after on one commit) is unachievable as written and was **declared N/A rather than satisfied with a number that would not have meant anything**, and THR-940's "≤60% of baseline" gate can be met or missed by luck alone (should be median-of-≥5, or judged on vitest's internal `import`/`tests` split, which its own Done-when #4 already asks for). Done-when #4 resolved by **deleting `vitest.config.isolated.ts`** — an 8-line stub invoked by nothing (`test` is a bare `vitest run`, no `--config` anywhere) and strictly *worse* than the real config: no `setupFiles`, no `plugins`, and **no `exclude`**, so running it would have swept `node_modules/`, `dist/` and every sibling worktree into the suite, while its stated purpose "node-only without jsdom overhead" is already the default. THR-940 names that file as "already exists as a seam" — it was not a usable one, and a comment on that ticket says so. Levers 3 and 4 continue as THR-940/THR-939 with their cost premise corrected. Full suite green (942 files, 14,596 tests); typecheck ratchet 3492 unchanged; `vite build` 9.81s; wiki-freshness clean.

✅ **THR-918 — Every design artifact entered the repo from its first draft, so brainstorming paid full handoff ceremony** (2026-08-01, Continuous Improvement) — `design-session` wrote every plan doc straight into `Docs/plans/` behind a `docs/plan-*` PR, correct for a doc about to become an executor contract and wrong for a concept rewritten five times in a day that may never reach an executor at all. **The cost was never compute** — THR-917 measured docs-only PRs at 30–60s with no tests — it was session ceremony and the implicit signal that a half-formed thought is a versioned artifact. Plan docs now carry two lifecycle stages: **exploratory** (Obsidian vault, no git/PR/CI/lint, rewrite freely) and **committed** (`Docs/plans/`, governance unchanged), with promotion triggered by exactly one event: the issue moving toward Ready for Dev — not length, not confidence, not session count. **The vault folder already existed and was already load-bearing, so "where?" was answered by stopping rather than inventing**: `Brainstorms/` holds 10 hand-curated drafts, has a documented frontmatter convention in `documentation-ownership.md`, and is **cited as a source by canon pages today** (`Docs/canon/cosmology.md` names `brainstorm-cosmological-symmetry.md` as its canonical iteration record, ×3) — which is simultaneously the evidence that a non-git path in a citation breaks nothing, so the discoverability question got measured rather than argued. **Discoverability answered by reading the consumers:** `lint:plan-doc` lints only *staged* files under `Docs/plans/`, `rebuild-plans-index` globs that same directory, and `check:process` invokes `lint:plan-doc --staged` — a vault draft is invisible to all three **by construction** and none requires a `Plan doc:` line to resolve. Exploratory issues therefore carry a **`Draft:`** line while `Plan doc:` stays reserved for a committed doc, which keeps THR-921's proposed promotion-time liveness gate valid instead of pre-broken. **Governance confirmed inapplicable against the authoritative file rather than assumed** — intent-judge scores the plan doc, design-audit writes into the plan-doc tail, `lint:plan-doc` lints `Docs/plans/`, the three-pillar rule gates the handoff; none can even run against a vault draft, so governance attaches *at promotion*, in full. **The Brainstorm companion is not weakened — it is the promotion product**, which is why `design-governance.md`'s companion requirement needed no edit and no contradiction was introduced. Loss risk stated rather than buried: the vault is not git-backed, an unpromoted draft has no history, and that is the accepted price of zero ceremony. **A fourth file was edited beyond the ticket's three** — `Docs/documentation-ownership.md`, the declared ownership authority — because Done-when 4 forbids surviving contradictions and it described the vault's layers without naming `Brainstorms/`. **The residual tension was filed, not silently left** (THR-944): grill-me synthesis still lands in `Docs/plans/` though it runs on exploratory work by definition, and its home is `Docs/canon/design-governance.md` — authoritative and outside this ticket's scope, where widening would have created the very contradiction Done-when 4 forbids. Docs-only track (THR-917): classifier returned empty, so `npm test` / typecheck / `vite build` were correctly not run; `check:generated-freshness`, `lint:plan-doc` and `check:impediment-ids` all pass.

✅ **THR-934 — Spawned encounters had no second chapter, and the ticket's stated cause was not the one that fired** (2026-08-01, Encounter Experience) — `?spawn` passed `courtPosition: 'the_first'` as a *notification-time override* and wrote nothing to the graph, so only the spawn-time notification carried it and every later tick re-derived visibility from the graph without it. **The ticket read the target as unthreaded** (`getVisibilityDepth(null) → 'none'`, so steps 2+ generate nothing) — but `collectThreadedAgents` already synthesizes a `the_first` entry for the ascendant's avatar, which is what `@hero` resolves to, so **the notification was generated every time**. The actual gate is that the synthetic entry stamps `attentionMode: 'auto_resolve'`, handing `buildEncounterNotification` a non-null `autoResolveTick`, which `shouldAutoOpenEncounterNotification` reads as "do not open now" — the beat existed and never surfaced, which is exactly why the symptom read as *silent resolution* rather than *no resolution*. Checking the stated cause before coding was again the whole job (verify-the-noun-before-the-verb): the fix the ticket proposed was right, the mechanism it gave for why was not, and the difference decides what the regression test may assert. The same synthetic entry carries `threadEdgeId: ''` and the Threads panel lists *real* edges, so there was no row to anchor the THR-664 badge to — **one cause, both reported symptoms**. `ensureDebugSpawnThread` upserts a real `the_first`/`pause` thread and, critically, **retunes** a pre-existing `auto_resolve` one, since `?seeded`'s Kael arrives on precisely that setting and a skip-if-present upsert would have inherited the thing suppressing the continuation. **The regression pins the mechanism, not the symptom** — asserting "a step-2 notification exists" would have passed before the fix, so the assertion is `autoResolveTick === null`, paired with a falsification twin that deletes the written edge and asserts the notification is present but *non-null*; red baseline confirmed with 4 of the new tests failing on the reverted production change. Live at 1920×1080 on the ticket's own `?spawn=` URL: commit step 1, one `__DEBUG.tick(1)`, step-2 stage pops unprompted, Vara carries a Threads row and the badge `"Snow on the Pass, step 2 of 2 · wavered — open encounter"`, 0 console errors. **One Done-when clause was filed rather than claimed** (THR-943): "clicking the badge reopens the stage" has no reachable state at `the_first`/`pause`, because dismissing the stage (Resume *or* Escape) resolves the notification and retires the badge with it. Full suite green; typecheck ratchet 3492 unchanged; `vite build` 10.37s; 30-tick CLI smoke reached tick 30 with 383 agents / 47 events. Unblocks THR-906 and THR-907.

✅ **THR-924 — Every multi-step encounter crashed the tick the moment it reached a fork** (2026-08-01, Encounter Experience) — `UnifiedActionTemplate.steps` is `ActionStepOrBranch[]`, and an `ActionStepBranch` carries its `reach` on each *variant*, never on itself. `fallbackContractFromTemplate` asserted that union away with `template.steps as readonly ActionStep[]`, then read `step.reach` off every entry — so a branch arrived at `defaultPoleForReach` with `reach === undefined` and `MORAL_AXIS_POLES_BY_REACH[undefined][0]` threw. **The cast is the whole defect:** the compiler knew the shape and was told not to look. **The blast radius was far wider than the fork-bearing template** — `phaseAscendantHandFilter` adapts *every* pending encounter notification in one unguarded loop, so a single fork-bearing encounter anywhere in the world threw out of the phase and the orchestrator caught it as "Tick crashed, returning previous state", reverting the tick for every other pending encounter as well. That is why `snow_on_the_pass` and `shrine_offering` were reported as crashing despite adapting cleanly in isolation: one root cause, four symptoms, with NFP #4's fail-soft loop converting a hard crash into an encounter that merely never advanced. **The ticket's stated hypothesis was wrong, and checking it before coding was the whole job** — it proposed a clobbered `reach` or a stale module-graph import; enumerating the five repro templates showed two carrying a step with no `reach` at all, naming the branch union immediately. Fix resolves a branch to its `fallback` (the arm `resolveStepDefinition` picks before any choice is recorded, and the idiom already used by `encounterCache`, `encounterEventNode`, and the encounter-stage adapters), and makes `defaultPoleForReach` degrade to a pole instead of throwing, since it runs inside the tick loop. **Only templates without encoded contract metadata walked the broken path** — one carrying `__encounter_contract_v1` in `illustrationAlt` is decoded verbatim — so the shipped `reputation.*` forks were never affected, and the regression test splits on that exported predicate rather than asserting a single beat-count rule across both paths. Coverage is a predicate over the live pool (THR-688 rule A), with both populations asserted non-empty so it cannot go vacuous. **Falsified rather than asserted:** reverting the fix turns the phase-level test red with the exact reported stack, and live in-browser on the ticket's `?spawn=` URL `__DEBUG.tick(8)` reports `ticksRun: 8, tick: 0` (eight ticks run, world frozen) against `tick: 8` with the fix. The 30-tick CLI smoke is explicitly **not** fix evidence — it behaves identically reverted, because the headless path never builds the notification shape that reaches the crash. Full suite **14572 green (941 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3492 unchanged**; `vite build` 10.14s; 30-tick CLI smoke reached tick 30 with 383 agents / 47 events. Browser-verify exempt: engine-only, no `src/components/` file touched (browser evidence gathered anyway, above).

✅ **THR-881 — The impediment log's primary key was never checked, and 15 numbers had collided** (2026-07-31, Continuous Improvement) — `merge=union` (THR-691) keeps both sides of a conflicting hunk, which is right for appended rows and wrong for their hand-assigned numbers; the generated-artifact gate only proved the dashboard matched its source, never that the source's keys were distinct. `check:impediment-ids` is now a blocking CI step, and the 15 collisions (oldest 2026-03-25) were repaired first-row-keeps-the-number so every existing prose cross-reference still resolves. The date-slug id migration was costed and declined — the check closes the hole before the merge, which is the invariant the scheme was wanted for.

✅ **THR-872 — The meeting's trait seeds finally land: four producers, no consumer, 366 descriptors discarded** (2026-07-31, Encounter Experience) — `MeetingEncounterResult.traitSeeds` was written by four authoring sources (legacy dilemmas in `meeting-content.ts`, the 167-template enriched library, spark-vision `traitGrants`, and THR-868's bond reception) and read by none: `createAgentFromMeeting` never touched the field, so every descriptor the meeting authored died at the graph boundary. The symptom was silent and universal — a freshly-created First holds no `has_trait` edges, so `generateBackstory`'s `{trait}` slot fell through to the hardcoded `'resolute'` for **every First ever met**, over the top of the five descriptors the player had just chosen. **The landing shape was the ticket's real question and it went to an additive node property, not to `has_trait` edges.** The seeds are free-text character description (`cold_clarity`, `market_eye`, `oath-keeper`) — 366 distinct values against a registered trait vocabulary that is namespaced (`trait.core.*`) and deliberately closed (THR-800). Landing them as traits would mean minting 366 definitions carrying none of the scoring or domain semantics that *define* a trait, or mapping-and-killing — discarding authored content to fit a vocabulary it was never written against (NFP #6). They land as `narrativeDescriptors` and surface in prose (NFP #5). **The consequence is documented at the write site because it is the next bug:** these values are not trait refs and must never reach `resolveTraitPredicate` or `validateTraitRefs`, which would register 366 dead refs — so `agentDetail` keeps them in a list separate from `getAgentTraitNames`. **A landing with no reader reproduces the bug one layer up**, so the reader ships in the same change: the character-sheet trait list at `intimate` knowledge (`allTraits`), and the backstory slot, where an earned trait still wins when one exists — descriptors fill only the case previously guaranteed to render the fallback. Interface-map row added and badged **LIVE** with dated evidence (1 write, 2 read). Landing is order-preserving and deduped; an unseeded First writes no property at all, matching THR-868's `quintessence` discipline. **The test enumerates the population from all four catalogs with each source asserted non-empty individually** — a single combined check would pass with three of the four dead, which is the vacuous-probe shape the ticket's own Done-when named. Full suite **14391 green (936 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3493 unchanged**; `vite build` 9.62s; 30-tick CLI smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events. Browser-verify exempt: engine-only, no `src/components/` file touched.

✅ **THR-850 — The executor lane's prompt mirror: a backup no audit read had rotted into a trap** (2026-07-31, Continuous Improvement) — `tb-opus-pickup`, the sole lane that claims/implements/ships every ticket, was filed as unmirrored. ✅ **THR-892 — Derived factor lines: the test panel stops repeating scene facts and starts reporting what varies** (2026-07-30, Encounter Experience) — Implements the variance rule Christian approved on the THR-883 mockup review: *a factor line earns its place only if it could have read differently on another run*. A static authored line reads identically every firing, so it informs no decision — it belongs in the prose, priced into `difficulty`. `buildNudgePhaseModel` now derives the panel from the broader game context: the actor's capability in the step's reach (always present, always `for` — the difficulty word beside it already carries the "this is hard" signal, so a low capability is reported by the *word*, not by flipping polarity), plus one line per named world modifier. **The load-bearing constraint was "one read path, never a parallel computation."** A panel that re-derived its own numbers would eventually disagree with the roll and quote the player a factor the roll never applied — so `computeResolutionModifiers` was refactored to emit a **named** `contributions` list from the *same* walk that produces its totals, and the derived lines are a pure projection of it. The refactor is behavior-preserving by construction: `computeEquipmentModifier` / `computeTraitBonus` / `computeTerrainModifier` now sum the contribution list they collect, with the per-item and total caps applied by trimming the overflowing tail so the emitted values sum to *exactly* the previously-returned number (all 30 pre-existing modifier tests pass untouched, including both cap tests). **Omens, doom stage and season derive nothing, and that is a finding rather than a gap** — `forecastAction` consumes only `ResolutionInput.actionModifiers`, which `computeResolutionModifiers` fills, and no omen/doom/season read exists anywhere in that pipeline; a line for them would name a cause the roll never applied, so they are recorded N/A with the read path cited rather than faked. **`ActionStep.carryoverFactorLines` is the one authored factor surface that survives the rule**, because it is keyed on a band the run actually rolled: resolved against `stepOutcomes[currentStep − 1]`, so step 0 never draws one and an unauthored band draws nothing rather than a fallback. A declared `forecastDelta` rides the existing named channel as `carryover:<outcome>` through `collectNudgeModifiers`, reaching **both** the panel floor and live resolution, and taking **zero** new rng — the draw it reads happened last step. Sentence templates live in `nudge-stage-content.ts` as half-sentences rather than `{label}: {value}` pairs, which is what makes canon rule 1 (source named *in* the sentence) structurally impossible to violate. Every line class carries a **falsification twin** — remove the source, the line must vanish — and the two THR-820 tests that asserted the panel is *exactly* the authored set were correctly broken and rescoped to the authored slice. The carryover-forecast test asserts `forecastInput.actionModifiers` rather than the resulting probability, because the capability-0 fixture sits on the 0.05 probability floor where a +0.1 modifier is absorbed: the floor is real behaviour, it just cannot witness the wiring. Full suite **14342 green (933 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3493 unchanged**; `vite build` 10.59s; 30-tick CLI smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events. Browser-verified at a genuine 1920×1080 on a worktree dev server (server identity proved by fetching the new module through Vite before asserting): the derived line **"Vara is oblivious in eye."** renders live at `nudge-factor-skill:eye` beside the exemplar's three authored lines, 0 console errors, no horizontal overflow.

✅ **THR-885 — Nudge card system: cards that cost in other currencies, change the world, and are dealt on world state** (2026-07-30, Encounter Experience) — Ticket B of the THR-883 authoring-framework split. Ships the `all_or_nothing` rider (The Gambit — widens both ends, sits *last* in `NUDGE_RIDER_PRIORITY` so a protective card in the same hand always wins), signed `detectionDelta` / `doomDelta` cost channels, card grants, two world-state hand filters (`requiresGroup`, `requiresFavor`), The Signature sphere discount, and a build-time grant-liveness gate. **The design finding is that five of the six dispatch hooks needed no new machinery at all.** Card grants are typed as `EncounterAftermathReactionEffect[]` and dispatched through the existing `applyEncounterAftermathReaction`, so The Omen, The Balm, The Cache, The Long Game and The Favor route to their owning systems through the doors `emit_omen` / `remove_condition` / `spawn_artifact` / `hidden_mark` / `favor_creation` already use — reusing the vocabulary is what keeps a card from minting a second path to a place that already has one. **The two exceptions were added to the owning module, not beside it, and each closed a real gap:** `assign_ambition` exists because reactive ambition templates had *no assignment path outside `ambitionTick`* (THR-812 / THR-726), so `assignAmbitionToActor` was extracted from the three in-phase copies of the node+edge write — that duplication *was* the bug; and `applyRawDetectionDelta` exists because every prior detection writer priced by `EncounterChoiceCost` band, which can only *raise* pressure, leaving The Veil with no channel to write through. **The discount is quoted and charged by one shared function** (`effectiveNudgeCost`, used by both the affordability check and `totalNudgeCost`) because showing a discounted card as affordable and then deducting the authored price is the bug a discount feature otherwise ships with; an authored-free card stays free, since free is a decision and not a number a discount arrives at. **The liveness test is deliberately self-falsifying** — the shipped corpus authors zero card grants (content is THR-883), so a sweep over it would print PASS while proving nothing; the test re-injects a dead ref and asserts the sweep catches it. Three interface-map rows added, all **deliberately not badged LIVE** with `deferralTicket: THR-883`, because badging a path nothing travels is the THR-614 error class. Full suite **14275 green (932 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3493 unchanged**; `vite build` 10.12s; 30-tick CLI smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events. **THR-886** filed for The Compulsion, the one hook not shipped: its host API needs the decision pipeline's `ScoredCandidate[]`, which aftermath cannot obtain, and faking them would have been exactly the parallel-path failure the plan forbids.

✅ **THR-884 — Setting envelopes: authors declare a kind of place, not a list of 20 subtypes** (2026-07-30, Encounter Experience) — Ticket A of the THR-883 authoring-framework split. The engine always gated templates per location (`locationSubtypes` → `encounterCache`); what failed was practice — placeless prose stamped with every subtype, which scene-built prose makes a lie. Ships the closed 8-class vocabulary + expansion table (`SETTING_CLASS_MAP`), a raw-entry `settings` field the converter expands (`locationTypes` demoted to the exact-subtype override), per-class `openings` compiled into a `{frag:opening}` set, per-card `fictionBySetting`, the validation suite, and a coverage-matrix generator. **The load-bearing constraint was "no second resolution mechanism":** `setting` joined `place`/`counterpartRole` as a third THR-573 identity axis, and `resolveSettingVariant` delegates to `resolveFragment` rather than reimplementing the fallback chain — so an opening and a card variant cannot disagree about what "no entry for this class" means. **The vocabulary covers the 20 *authorable* subtypes, not all ~50 `LocationSubtype` values** — the ~30 worldgen overlay kinds (wonders, lairs, anomalies) are deliberately unclassed, because folding them in would invent coverage no encounter targets (the THR-844 dead-vocabulary failure in a new place); they take the `'*'` default rather than a blank. **The corpus sweep is vacuous today and says so** — content is paused behind THR-883, so no shipped template declares `settings`, and a corpus-only test would print PASS while checking nothing; the completeness rule lives in an exported `validateSettingEnvelope` with five falsification cases proving each guard fires now, leaving the sweep as a live regression guard for when content lands. All three read sites (prose enrichment, the instantiation trace, the player-facing hand) resolve through the cache's own exported `locationTypeFromProperties`, so the class the prose binds to is the class the template was filtered in under. The generated matrix reports **440 drawable templates** across 8×8 cells with no cell at or below 2, 22 templates drawable only at unclassed subtypes, and flags `encounter` at 71% sphere-kind cards. Full suite **14240 green (931 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3493 unchanged**; `vite build` 10.06s; 30-tick CLI smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events. The pinned fragment-axis set was widened deliberately at the pin. Browser-verify substitution stated in the commit body: the one `src/components/` file is data-threading with zero authored consumers.

✅ **THR-874 — `?firstunmet` dev entry: the Meet-The-First beat is reachable from a URL for the first time** (2026-07-30, Encounter Experience) — Every browser Done-when on the meeting surface was unrunnable: bare `?view=game` supplies no ascendant identity (and CLAUDE.md wrongly named it the MeetTheFirst route), while `?view=game&seeded` pre-bonds The First. Split the single `preSeeded` flag into `seedFirst` / `seedTestPackage`; unbonding The First proved necessary but not sufficient, since the auto-trigger also requires a settlement and the ascendant starts at a `shrine` — so the dev entry relocates the avatar (`devPlaceAvatarAtSettlement`, fail-soft) rather than loosening the production allowlist, which was also de-duplicated into the exported `MEETING_SETTLED_LOCATION_SUBTYPES`. Verified: `getMeetingState()` → `beat: 'sensing'`.

✅ **THR-869 — Ascendant sheet & bar: sphere/reach axis legibility fix** (2026-07-30, UI Visual Overhaul — Design System v1) — Christian reported the character sheet's "Primary Matter / Secondary Mind" reading as a contradiction against the left bar's "Primary Stone / Secondary Gold / Secondary Iron". **Not a contradiction — two orthogonal axes (spheres, reaches) neither of which named itself**, compounded by three real divergences: the sheet listed all 8 reaches in fixed catalog order with the god's primary buried 7th and no rank marking, fed from frozen day-one `startingDomainAffinities` through the **mortal** tier ladder, while the bar showed live ranked progression off `getAscendantProgress`. ✅ **THR-667 — faction notifications anchored to the faction's own thread row** (2026-07-30, Attention Tier Model) — The follow-up THR-666 named in a source comment when it parked `faction_founded`, `faction_dissolved` and `faction_rank_changed` in `ALWAYS_GLOBAL_EVENT_TYPES`: faction news stayed loud by explicit deferral, not oversight. **The anchor surface already existed and needed no invention** — `ThreadsPanel` renders a `Factions` section whose `CompactThreadRow` already branched on `category === 'faction'` for sphere, territory and member counts, and `collectThreadedAgents` is keyed by thread *target*, so threaded factions were already inside the gate's own set. A single `node.category === 'agent'` ternary on the per-row badge lookup was the whole distance between a faction notice and its row; the ticket's instruction to "reuse that mechanism, do not invent a second one" was satisfiable almost literally. **The load-bearing decision is ordering, because `faction_rank_changed` carries both an `actorId` and a `factionId`** — the promoted member, and the order they were promoted in — so "which row" is a genuine choice. `ALWAYS_GLOBAL` wins outright (founding and collapse are world-scale: a faction entering or leaving the world changes the map for everyone, threaded or not), then the new `FACTION_ANCHORED_EVENT_TYPES` set, then the pre-existing mortal path. **The fall-through is what keeps this from being a suppression regression:** a faction-scoped beat whose faction is *unthreaded* drops through to the mortal branch rather than to `suppress`, so a player holding the member's thread but not the faction's — the common case — still gets the news on the member's row. **The gate's return type had to change shape, and that is the transferable finding.** The router derived the destination row from `event.actorId`, which was correct only while "diverted" implied "about a mortal"; a faction beat carries both ids, so `ActorRouting` (a bare `'global' | 'entity' | 'suppress'` string) became `NotificationRouting`, a discriminated union whose `entity` case carries `anchorId` + `anchorKind`. The decision and its anchor now travel together and the push site stopped guessing — `EntityNotice.agentId` became `anchorId` + `anchorKind` for the same reason, since a faction notice filed under `agentId` would have been a lie. **A disjointness test pins the two event-type sets apart**, because `ALWAYS_GLOBAL` is checked first: a type listed in both would read as anchored in the source while behaving as global forever — exactly the silent-dead-path shape this ticket removed. `isFactionNode` deliberately mirrors `isMortalAgentNode` (reading `actorType`, never a `category` field `GraphNode` does not have), and guards the anchor against a `factionId` that no longer resolves, failing soft to the mortal path. Tooltip wording is anchor-aware because *"a life turns"* is the wrong sentence for an institution: `NOTICE_FACTION_CATEGORY_LABEL` overrides fall back to the agent labels, so a category needs a faction entry only once the agent phrasing grates. **Browser-verified end to end through the real pipeline**, not a mounted fixture: three Merchant Consortium members parked one decay-tick above the 0.3/0.6/0.85 rank thresholds, `phaseFactionReputationDecay` fired the demotions across `window.__DEBUG.tick()`, and 6 notices accumulated on the faction row reading *"Their ranks shift: Vann has been demoted to Apprentice in The Merchant Consortium. and 5 more — open the faction's thread"* (`data-notice-badge-category="social"`, count 6); clicking it cleared the badge to 0 and left the faction row `aria-selected="true"`. Screenshot at 1920×1080 with `innerWidth/innerHeight` measured and `scrollWidth === innerWidth` (no horizontal overflow); console **0 errors**, 42 warnings all pre-existing baseline noise (GraphSchema `belongs_to`/`region`, `THREE.Clock` deprecation, WebGL `texImage3D`). Full suite **14124 green (923 files)**, +21 from this ticket; typecheck ratchet **3493 unchanged**; `vite build` 12.59s; 30-tick CLI smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events; wiki-freshness OK across 23 pages. **THR-862** filed: `faction_founded` is emitted for both genuine founding *and* "agent joined a faction" (with a code comment conceding the mislabel), so the join beat cannot be anchored while it shares a type — deliberately not reclassified here, since silently changing what a shared type means is how the next reader gets surprised.

✅ **THR-842 — the two skips: recording which vacuous merge gate we accept** (2026-07-29, Repo Health) — The GitHub Actions billing block cleared overnight (item 1 discharged by the 2026-07-29 grooming verdict, which proved a *real execution* of the required check rather than merely a green one), leaving the part no outage fixes: **the design call on gate topology.** GitHub has no setting to stop a `SKIPPED` required check from satisfying branch protection, and the naive response — fail closed on any skip — is unavailable, because the skip is **load-bearing**: every orchestrator sweep and briefing refresh is docs-only, and all **15** most recent `ci.yml` runs on `main` show `Test · Typecheck · Build: skipped` for that entirely correct reason. So the recorded rule is the narrow one: **a skip may only ever come from a decision, never from an absence**, with the discriminator being the *gating* job — `Detect code changes` reading `success` means the filter chose to skip; anything else means the check never inspected the change and THR-768's guard step fails it closed. **The verdict names its residual risk instead of claiming closure**: nothing mechanically asserts that a code-carrying diff cannot produce a skip — the guarantee rests on one YAML `if` no test exercises — so the accepted mitigation is operational (`pull-work`'s stand-down on `check:actions`, and its post-arming rollup read), with a review trigger on the next edit to that condition or a third incident. **Item 2 needed an enabler, not a workaround.** No full gate run on a `main` commit existed to retro-verify `ae5990ab` / `c963671a` / `6534a3d8`, and forcing one meant fabricating a code change purely to trip the path filter — so `ci.yml` gains `workflow_dispatch`, with the paths-filter step skipped on that event (a dispatch payload carries no diff base for it to read; skipping leaves the job `success`, which correctly keeps the vacuous-gate guard quiet) and the `check` job running unconditionally. This PR then discharges the literal Done-when for free: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is a non-doc path, so the filter reports `code: true` and the suite runs on the PR *and* again on the push to `main` whose history contains all three merges. Full suite **14013 green (918 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3496 unchanged**; `vite build` 10.13s. Browser-verify exempt: CI workflow + docs only, no runtime UI. Engine smoke N/A — nothing under `src/`. Verdict doc: `Docs/plans/2026-07-29-thr-842-skipped-required-check-verdict.md`; canon pointer in `Docs/canon/process.md`; impediment #290.

✅ **THR-844 — the secrets the world could never find out: 67 of 115 reveal-family names matched zero templates** (2026-07-29, Action System & Unlocks) — A hidden mark's `revealFamilies` decides which encounters can ever surface it, matched by raw `templateId.startsWith(family)` — so a family only worked if the author happened to write a real template-id prefix. Measured against the shipped 672-template pool: **67 of the 115 distinct literals matched zero templates**, and **42 of 136 authored entries named only dead ones** — placed, decayed, unrevealable by construction, for as long as the feature has existed. THR-661 hit three of these while choosing families for the curse mark; this is the sweep. **The dead names are the diagnosis, not just the symptom**: they are overwhelmingly thematic — `investigation`, `oracle`, `guild`, `duel`, `shrine`, `spy`, `magistrate`, `river` — which is authors writing a *tag vocabulary* against an engine that wanted prefixes. `investigation` alone is the corpus's most-used family at 65 uses and never once fired. **So the fix is an alias layer, not a rename.** Renaming ~100 authored entries to real prefixes would have been a large destructive diff that discarded authorial intent (what prefix means "oracle"?) and left the class free to recur; `REVEAL_FAMILY_ALIASES` instead resolves a family to the prefixes it *means*, and an unaliased family resolves to itself, so every name that already worked (`social`, `tavern`, `borderland`, `faction`, `hex.`, the faction-rank families) matches byte-identically (NFP #6). A family name is now a declared thing that can be validated — which is the point. **The guard was falsified, not assumed**: `revealFamilyLiveness.test.ts` asserts that every authored family, every engine-planted family and every prefix *inside the alias table* matches ≥1 live template, that no entry loses its last live family, and that no alias matches >25% of the pool (a family revealing on everything is as useless as one revealing on nothing); disabling alias resolution turns **70 of its 197 assertions red**. Population is pinned before any assertion, since a guard over an empty corpus passes vacuously and reads exactly like one that works. **Ten existing tests had to be repaired, and that is the finding underneath the finding** — they paired the family `investigation` with invented ids like `investigation.audit`, passing on a prefix match between two strings that existed only in the test file. The THR-112 *liveness contract test* was among them, asserting that marked agents prefer investigation encounters against a template the game cannot draw. They now use `social.investigate_reputation`. Also: `FAILURE_ARTIFACT_REVEAL_FAMILIES` (THR-571 C1's no-dead-air fallback) was a third narrower than it read and is now live in all three entries, values unchanged; `checkMarkReveals`'s misleading `encounterFamily` parameter is renamed to `templateId`. **One trap deliberately left open and documented rather than papered over**: encounter-seed `encounterFamily` is still matched raw, so the two vocabularies have diverged, and the guide now says so instead of leaving the next author to rediscover it. Full suite **14013 green (918 files)**, +211 from this ticket; typecheck ratchet **3496 unchanged**; `vite build` 12.43s; 30-tick CLI smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events; wiki-freshness OK across 23 pages. Browser-verify exempt: engine, content-data and docs only — no file under `src/components/`, `src/views/`, `index.css` or HexMapV2 touched.

🔵 **THR-838 pass 2 (partial, in flight) — the camp maintenance pair, and a reachability guard that had never once fired** (2026-07-28, Encounter Experience) — Two more templates migrated: `ward_the_camp` (168→1088 authored words, vagueness **2.38→0.00**, its only failing detector) and `sharpen_blades` (149→1051 words, abstraction **3.36→0.19**), the same camp night as pass 1's cluster approached from maintenance rather than rest. Each carries per-step hands of 5–6 cards spanning ≥4 spheres with a sphere-less common option and a zero-cost trait card on a live Core ref (`core_integrity.virtue`, `core_humility.virtue`), fragments covering all six `StepOutcome` bands, both factor-line signs, and all five afterimages. Batch detector failures **30→29**; hands **3→5** of 48. **The pass's real finding is in the checklist, not the content.** `checkNudgeHand`'s THR-821 reachability rule — the one deciding whether a hand *does anything*, since a step the drawing actor has no capability in floors at `PROBABILITY_FLOOR` and stays floored while the player spends essence — built its reach set as `new Set([template.reach, ...template.steps.map(s => s.reach)])` and then asked whether it contained `step.reach`. The step being iterated is always one of `template.steps`, so `offReach` was **unconditionally false** and the rule had passed vacuously over every template ever run through it, including the three pass 1 certified against it. This is the project's standing `vacuous_probe_empty_population` shape at the level of a single boolean: a guard whose green is indistinguishable from absence. **The replacement binds the ceiling to a population that can violate it** — `OPEN_DRAW_ATTENTION_TIER` (`background`), the tier meaning ambient content a mortal draws by being where it is, with no selection on reach, role or faction, so every step is off-reach for most of the roster and the ceiling binds across the board; above that tier the audience is author-chosen and the checklist cannot see it, so it defers rather than guessing. **Swapping one predicate for another earns exactly one thing: an obligation to demonstrate the new one can fail.** Three liveness cases pin it — fires on an open-draw step above the ceiling, quiet on the identical step below it, defers at `notable` — and the first is **red against the old predicate**, making it a genuine regression guard rather than a restatement. All five migrated templates sit at 0.05–0.10 against the 0.45 ceiling, so the repair changed no content. ✅ **THR-618 — the essence bridge: a god's power is rooted in the land their people work** (2026-07-28, M3: Dynamic Economy) — Mortal Economy P4's last open item. The five divine economic verbs shipped 2026-07-22 and the Flow Web extraction checkpoint was decided 2026-07-22 (**defer** — the second consumer shipped comfortably without the primitive); what remained was the *essence bridge*, and the checkpoint's own evidence table was the diagnosis: `essenceSources.ts` imported nothing from `resourceEconomy.ts` and referenced no `stockTier` concept, so the two webs sat on the same map and never touched. A **typed** essence source now drifts its sanctity each tick from the stock tiers of the goods at its host location that share its `sphereAffinity` — a Spirit shrine off its valley's pearls, a Matter nexus off its ore and stone — weighted by class `baseValue`, `surplus +1 / adequate 0 / scarce −1`. **Two asymmetries are the design, not clamps.** Upward drift stops at `ECON_SANCTITY_NURTURE_CEILING` (0.5), deliberately below `SANCTITY_FLOWERING_THRESHOLD` (0.6): the land readies a source and **only a Sanctify cast flowers it**. Without that bound a well-sited shrine would flower unattended and the Build verb would become decoration. Withering has **no** floor above zero and stacks with the contested drain in the same tick, so the world takes away more than it gives — which is precisely what makes tending and defending a source worth the player's attention. **Untyped sources are excluded by construction, not by a default.** A migrated, unbuilt place of power has no `sphereAffinity` and stays on the legacy alignment-distributed income term; drifting its sanctity would change income for a save that has done nothing, breaking THR-611's load-bearing NFP #6 contract. Pinned by a 100-tick test on a doubly-surplus location. **The read is the derived per-resource `stockTier`, deliberately not `resourceBalance` and not `prosperity`** — the same coarse tier the Livelihood line renders — so the number the player is shown and the number the divine economy acts on cannot drift apart. The first interface-row draft declared `computeSanctitySustenance` at the producing phase and pinned itself 🔴 LEAKED; correcting the mechanism to the node-prop that actually crosses the boundary is the same trap `economy-verbs-answered` records one row above. **No new tick phase, node type, edge type, or income channel** — one signed number per source per tick, applied inside the `controls`-edge walk `recomputeControlledSourceTiers` was already running. Every structural miss returns a zero-drift result carrying a `reason` (`untyped` / `no-host` / `no-matching-goods` / `ceiling`), so the debug surface distinguishes *drawing nothing* from *drawing zero*. Content: `SUSTENANCE_PROSE`, per-Sphere × polarity, plain register. UI: one sentence appended to the Livelihood line when the location hosts a **discovered**, typed, non-desecrated source **and** grows goods of that Sphere — guards mirroring the engine's exactly, so the sentence never claims a bargain the drift is not making; DebugPanel Essence Sources tab gains a per-source `land:` line. `__DEBUG.getEssenceSources()` returns a `sustenance` block and finally gains the `.d.ts` entry it was missing entirely. 22 tests (4 CONTRACT). Full suite **13707 green (912 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3497 unchanged**; `vite build` 10.30s; 30-tick engine smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events; wiki-freshness OK across 23 pages; interface row `economy-sustains-essence-sources` 🟢 LIVE. Browser-verified at a genuine 1920×1080 (Playwright — Browser-verify substitution: unattended run, the Browser pane cannot composite headless): the Livelihood panel renders *"Luxuries glut the stalls… The offerings come freely here, and the holy ground answers them."* and its withering counterpart, no horizontal overflow, 1 console error (a pre-existing `localhost:3001/api/tts/health` connection refusal, unrelated). State assertion driven through the **served browser bundle**: two controlled Spirit shrines over 60 ticks — the surplus valley climbed 0.30 → 0.50 and stopped at the ceiling still `dormant`, the scarce valley fell 0.30 → 0.00, first tick reporting `econNurtured: 1, econWithered: 1`.

✅ **THR-832 batch 2 — the nudge cards have pictures, and the review that caught the bad one is not a gate** (2026-07-28, Encounter Experience) — THR-777 shipped the manifest, the resolve chain, the UI wiring and the integrity gate, and batch 1 generated all 48 fate plates; nudge art was entirely un-generated, so `NudgePhaseShell`'s lookup — wired since WS4 — resolved nothing and **every** card rendered the gradient tile. ✅ **THR-820 — the test panel reads the encounter now, not a constant nobody rendered** (2026-07-27, Encounter Experience) — The WS1 authoring checklist requires per-step **test panel data**: a reach *purpose line* (≤`REACH_PURPOSE_MAX_WORDS` 4 words, plain — what the step is *testing*) and `FACTOR_LINES_MIN`–`FACTOR_LINES_MAX` (2–4) **factor lines**, each concrete and each naming its source. `ActionStep` carried neither. WS0 added `nudges`, `traitVariants` and the rider machinery; no `purposeLine`, no `factorLines` — so there was **no path from an authored encounter to the panel**. The golden exemplar authored both regardless, as fixture-local constants (`EXEMPLAR_REACH_PURPOSE_LINES` / `EXEMPLAR_FACTOR_LINES`, `darkhollow-vault-exemplar.ts:332`/`:342`) consumed only by `nudgeModel.test.ts`. **This is the `optional-field-no-writer` failure mode pointed the other way** — the *authoring* side existed and the *storage* did not — and its diagnostic signature is a green test asserting a field no surface consumes: the exemplar read as compliant while `EncounterStageTestPanelModel.purposeLine` sat declared and permanently `undefined`, rendering nothing at all. **Shipped option 1 (the plan's evident intent) rather than option 2 (the cheaper retreat).** The ticket offered both: add the schema, or rule that `forecast_factors` *is* the factor-line field and delete the checklist's ask. Option 2 was rejected because the checklist names counts and a "names its source" rule that a bare string tuple cannot express — retreating would have quietly reduced the panel to whatever the contract adapter happened to expose. `ActionStep.purposeLine?: string` and `ActionStep.factorLines?: readonly StepFactorLine[]` (`{ text, polarity }`) ship additive-optional, so a step declaring neither renders reach + difficulty exactly as before, which is every pre-nudge template. **Polarity becomes authored rather than inferred.** `buildNudgePhaseModel` prefers `step.factorLines` and renders each line at its declared sign; absent them it falls back to the contract's `beat.forecast_factors`, which carries no sign, so those lines stay `neutral`. `neutral` therefore stays in the `FactorPolarity` union rather than being removed as the ticket speculated — it is the honest reading of an unsigned pool that still carries every un-migrated template, not a hedge, and its doc comment now says which of the three sources can and cannot produce it. **`source` deliberately did not become a struct field.** The spec's canon rule 1 puts the cause *in the sentence* ("The mason cut his mark beside the third pin"), exactly as a trait-derived `TraitVariant.factorLine` names its trait; a structured `source` invites a label rendered beside the line, which is the key:value-is-unfinished-UX pattern the project rejects. Recorded in the type's doc comment so the next author does not re-propose it. **Content migrated, not duplicated:** both constants are deleted with a comment at the old site explaining why they must not return, and the exemplar's step 1 gains a fourth line (`'The vault is one room, and one room is quickly swept.'`, `for`) so **both** signs appear on every step — a step whose lines all cut one way is an assertion rather than a weighing, and the exemplar is the reference authors copy. That line also earns the existing `criticalSuccessAfterimage`, which already had them sweeping the floor behind them. **The tests were rebuilt to be capable of failing.** `nudgeModel.test.ts` now reads the step schema instead of the constants (and collects the lines into `exemplarProse()` for the register/vagueness/annotation sweeps, which the constants had bypassed); new `nudgeStage.test.ts` assertions run against `buildNudgePhaseModel` **output** driven by the real exemplar, pin the population first (`authored.length > 0` — two empty arrays compare equal), assert no authored line renders `neutral`, and cover the un-migrated fallback path separately. **Falsified rather than assumed:** reverting the adapter's two wiring lines turns exactly the two new tests red and leaves the fallback test green. Both wiki pages whose `sources` glob matches `src/types/unifiedAction.ts` were updated in the same PR rather than exempted — the encounters manual's nudge-hand section already enumerated the additive-optional schema and is the natural home. Full suite **13582 green (903 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3497 unchanged**; `vite build` 10.08s; 30-tick engine smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events; wiki-freshness OK across 23 pages. Browser-verified at 1920×1080 by mounting `NudgePhaseShell` over the running app (the exemplar is registered in no pool by design, so the stage is unreachable from a running game): panel reads *Eye · Read the lock · STEEP*, the `for` line renders `rgba(134,239,172,0.75)` and both `against` lines `rgba(248,113,113,0.7)` — two distinct colours where every authored line was previously one — 0 console errors, no horizontal scroll.

✅ **THR-821 — the nudges were never inert; they were staged on mortals the feature cannot reach** (2026-07-27, Encounter Experience) — THR-775's browser pass read `FORECAST Doomed p=0.050` on seven seeded mortals running the golden exemplar's `steep` step, found no card combination moved it, and filed the question as two candidates wanting different fixes: *the exemplar is deliberately brutal* (content) or *seeded mortals genuinely lack capability in most reaches* (tuning). **Measurement on seeds 42/99 says neither, and the correction is to the population rather than to any constant.** The seven agents were `npc_*` — all `ambient` tier — and `npcSeeding.ts:276-287` creates ambient nodes with **no `domainCapabilities` property at all**: 0 of 351 (seed 42) and 0 of 459 (seed 99) carry one, so `computeRawScore` returns 0 and `sigmoid(0) = 0.018`. That alone produces `p=0.050`, which is `PROBABILITY_FLOOR` exactly. But those agents also **cannot reach the nudge stage at any capability**: the stage is attended-only (`story_beat`), and `resolveEffectiveTier` (`attentionTier.ts:39`) returns `'invisible'` for a null or `dormant` court position, with `story_beat` surviving only at `retinue`/`the_first`. The forecast was telling the truth; the debug panel had staged it on agents outside the feature's audience — the *verify-the-noun-before-the-verb* failure in its measurement form. **For the audience that can actually be attended, the exemplar is fine.** `spotlight` agents (14/seed, all carrying capabilities) sit at capability p25 **0.973** / p50 **0.999**, and **98.2%** of their `(agent, reach)` pairs already clear the floor *unaided* on the exemplar's step 0 (d=0.45), 94.6–98.2% on its `severe` step 1 (d=0.60). Candidate 1 is refuted on measurement, not argument. **The real gap is narrower than either candidate, and it is an authoring constraint.** A mortal the player has just threaded lands at `notable` (`NOTABLE_THRESHOLD` 10 against `IMPORTANCE_PLAYER_ACTION` 3, so ~4 player actions), and `generateRoleCapabilities` gives that tier a steep internal spread: primary reach 0.310–0.881, secondary 0.119–0.500, **other 0.027–0.119**. Against a step at 0.45 in a non-primary/secondary reach, that cohort floors and **stays** floored through the entire hand — 0% clear unaided, 0% with two cards (+0.22), 0% at the documented `±0.20` `actionModifiers` cap, and 0% with the full authored 0.37. A hand that cannot move the forecast word is decorative: the player spends essence and watches nothing change. **Deliberately shipped no change to `PROBABILITY_FLOOR` (0.05) or the sigmoid (`SIGMOID_MIDPOINT` 10 / `SIGMOID_K` 0.4).** They are load-bearing for the entire resolution ladder — every encounter in the game, not just nudge-bearing ones — and THR-571's measured `success_at_cost`-dominant calibration (45–60%) rides on them; raising the floor to make one feature's cards visible would re-tune every outcome band. The shipped step population does not need it either: difficulty p50 is **0.26**, and only 240 of 1232 steps sit at `steep` or worse. **The count that reframes the whole ticket: zero shipped steps carry `nudges[]`.** The only nudge-bearing template in the repo is `NUDGE_GOLDEN_EXEMPLAR`, deliberately registered nowhere, so the "difficulty distribution of shipped nudge-bearing steps" the Done-when asks for is an *empty population* — THR-778/WS5 is what creates it. That is why the deliverable is a constraint WS5 inherits rather than a fix to existing content: `NUDGE_OFF_REACH_MAX_DIFFICULTY = 0.45` (the `steep` band floor, so the rule reads in the vocabulary the author already sees) in the authoring-side module that stays out of the client bundle, written into `nudge-authoring-spec.md` — the one contract **both** authoring skills load — as the rule that decides whether a hand does anything at all, and pinned by three tests over the real `computeResolutionThreshold` so it cannot rot when a constant elsewhere moves. The rule is stated as a boundary, not a prohibition: a step that *wants* to be `steep`/`severe` is fine if gated to actors who plausibly hold the reach, which is exactly what the exemplar does by drawing a thief into an `eye`/`shadow` vault. `Docs/canon/rulebook.md` § *The nudge* gains the honest line the surviving floor requires — *you are bending a mortal's odds, not substituting your competence for theirs* — with the matching clause on the always-load quick-reference card. Measurement kept runnable as `npm run measure:nudge-headroom`; write-up at `Docs/audits/2026-07-27-thr-821-nudge-headroom.md`. One residue filed rather than absorbed: **THR-827** — `ResolutionInput.actionModifiers` is documented "capped at ±0.20" while `computeResolutionThreshold` clamps only the *result*, and the exemplar's playable hand already sums to ~0.37, so the two readings give the nudge model very different ceilings just as WS5 begins authoring against one. Full suite **13565 green (903 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3500 unchanged**; `vite build` 10.12s; 30-tick engine smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events; wiki-freshness OK across 23 pages. ✅ **THR-793 — the repo root is three files, and the check that missed it can no longer pass from memory** (2026-07-27, Continuous Improvement) — `Docs/ops/weekly-hygiene-2026-07-22.md` reported *"no orphan root-level markdown"* as a clean check while `ls -1 *.md` at the root returned **16 orphans**, all untouched since March. ✅ **THR-815 — the guild economy runs for the first time** (2026-07-27, Encounter Experience) — THR-810 measured guild reputation gain at exactly **zero** and established it was unfed rather than mis-tuned; THR-814 fixed two mechanical blockers and measured the dominant one: faction membership is seeded overwhelmingly onto `ambient` NPCs (**225 of 227**) while `phaseAgentDecision`, the phase that generates guild-quest candidates, iterates `individual` actors at `spotlight` tier only — so **2 of 227 members could reach the draw path at all**, and no scoring, reward, or gate change could reach the rest. That is why all three of THR-814's candidate routing rules and all three of THR-810's tuning levers were void. **This ticket implements the routing rule THR-814 chose.** Because the attention-tier model's whole premise is that ambient actors are *not* simulated individually, content that reaches them must resolve at the tier that **is** — the faction node. `src/engine/factionMemberWork.ts` sweeps from `phaseFactionActions` (which already runs for all 49 faction nodes and already owns `commission_quest`) on its own `FACTION_MEMBER_WORK_INTERVAL = 6` gate, independent of the faction-action interval, and settles one authored job per selected off-loop member. **It re-uses the attended path rather than paralleling it:** rank access comes from the same `getAccessibleTemplates` (exported for this, not copied — two copies of that predicate would drift, and a drifted `encounterAccess` prefix is exactly the `merchant_consortium` defect THR-814 found), and payout from the same `processFactionEncounterReputation`, which gained one optional `rewardScale` parameter so rank bonus, alignment multiplier and completion bonus stay on a single code path. `FACTION_MEMBER_WORK_REWARD_SCALE = 0.5` keeps unattended work from out-earning a watched encounter, which would otherwise invert the game's attention economy. **Two selection rules are load-bearing, and the second was found by measurement rather than reasoning.** The window **rotates** with the pass counter, because filling it from the head every pass is precisely the positional starvation THR-814 had just found at the encounter cap stage — same failure shape, ruled out by construction. And it is **proportional** to membership (`FACTION_MEMBER_WORK_MEMBER_FRACTION = 0.15`, clamped 2–8): the flat cap written first made per-member cadence scale *inversely* with guild size, and the sweep showed the 45-member Merchant Consortium topping out at 0.765 against an apex of 0.85 while the 3-member Underking's Court saturated at 1.000 — the largest guilds, which carry the most authored content, were the ones structurally unable to reach their own apex tiers. **Measured on seed 42 / medium / 150 ticks, before → after:** reputation gains **0 → 449** (+32.575 total across **185 distinct memberships**), **944 jobs resolved faction-side** with 462 successes and **135 promotions**, apex holders **0 → 33**, `>=0.60` no longer collapsing (72 → 66 where the baseline fell 72 → 33), and rank-blocked templates **21 → 0**. `npm run sweep:rank-reach` **exits 0 and is now a live gate**, after three consecutive tickets in which its non-zero exit was the correct reading. **Cost is 0.109 ms/tick amortized** (0.655 ms per pass over 215 memberships) — stated because NFP #7 is the axis on which promoting members to spotlight, at ~14× the per-tick decision cost, was rejected. **UI pillar decided, not skipped:** only a rank change surfaces, as the `faction_rank_changed` event the decay side of this economy already emits for demotions; 227 memberships' worth of routine errands would drown the feed, so individual jobs stay in one aggregate `faction_member_work` trace per faction per pass, and the event id carries faction + actor + tick rather than repeating the still-open THR-781 collision. **Content pillar** is a reported register rather than a witnessed one — an ambient member has no scene to narrate, so the prose says the world tells you what already happened somewhere you were not looking. **Two findings filed rather than absorbed.** The five templates the sweep still cannot reach are **not** a rank-reachability failure: Builders' Fellowship holds **zero members** in every run because `pickFactionForNpc` takes the *first* faction matching a role's preferred type and six definitions share `factionType: 'guild'` — the same first-match starvation shape a third time — filed as **THR-816**, and the sweep now reports that class as `unowned`, distinct from `blocked`, so an empty guild stops being counted as an unreachable ladder. Second, the `encounter-health` completion floor moved **0.78 → 0.70**, and only after the A/B justified it: attributed to this change by stash-A/B, narrowed to seed 137 alone on the exact harness (mean 0.8067 → 0.7688, seeds 42 and 999 identical to the digit), and confirmed benign by inspecting every unresolved action in both arms — all ordinary encounters 0–1 steps in, nothing stalled or abandoned, 5 → 8 in-flight out of 20 → 22 started. A live guild economy shifts which member holds each faction's top standing, leadership feeds `getLeaderBias`, and the world diverges; at ~20 actions per seed one action is worth 5 points of rate. Full suite **13502 green (901 files)**; typecheck ratchet **3500 unchanged**; `vite build` 12.41s; 30-tick engine smoke reached tick 30 with 387 agents / 50 events.
