✅ THR-738 (live verification — DONE) — the phantom-Done class was proven dead rather than assumed dead. THR-74 had been swept to Done ×2–3 in one day by references that only *mentioned* it, including a sentence documenting the discipline; the repo half (PR #823) line-anchored our own workflow, and Christian disabled Linear's native auto-close on 2026-07-25 (per-team **Workflows & automations → Pull request and commit automations**, not the Settings → Integrations → GitHub path this file and ~20 briefs had wrongly recorded). Two settings changed by two parties with no test between them is exactly the shape of a fix that looks done and isn't, so this pass ran the live end-to-end proof against a throwaway scratch issue (THR-765, parked in `Idea` + assigned so it could never enter the pickup queue). **PR #836 (negative control)** fired all three vectors simultaneously — bare id in the branch name *and* the PR title, close keyword inside a prose sentence — and left the scratch issue untouched: a single `stateHistory` entry with `endedAt: null`, `completedAt: null`, both auto-close runs green and logging `No Linear issues referenced — nothing to close`. **PR #837 (positive control)**, on a branch with no `thr-` prefix and a title with no bare id so the standalone keyword line was the only possible signal, closed it: `Issues to close (→ Done): THR-765` → `✅ THR-765 → Done`, with the second run correctly reporting `already closed — skipping` (idempotency confirmed). The negative control is load-bearing precisely because our own workflow was *provably incapable* of acting on it — checked pre-merge against the shipped helper, `extractCloseableIssueIds` returned `[]` while the native-shaped detector still matched `THR-765` — so the issue surviving isolates the native integration as genuinely disabled, not merely unexercised. PR linking still fires (both PRs and commits attached to the scratch issue), which is the intended end state: links without auto-move.
✅ THR-731 (PR 1, band spawner) — companies got opposition their own size. Factions now field **bands**: three to six of their own named members, mustered from a colocated cluster and sent out as an ordinary `faction_band` company (THR-74), marked `bandRole`/`bandFactionId`. "Ordinary" is load-bearing — `isCompanyNode` accepts a band, so `phaseGroups` moves, frays and dissolves it unchanged, and its members are real agents whose deaths are real graph deaths. Two substrate corrections against the plan, both grep- and runtime-verified: the specified **lair raider** trigger cannot fire (a lair mints exactly one named elite ever, monster factions carry no `member_of` roster — 13 lairs / 0 elites at tick 0), deferred to THR-767 with the guild path shipped instead as the ticket's founding assassins-guild fantasy; and the plan's `BAND_SPAWN_LAIR_STAGE` names a numeric stage the lair system doesn't have (it gates on `lairTier`). Band eligibility deliberately bypasses `isGroupEligibleAgent`'s `spotlightTier` check — that gate is an attention budget for player-facing formation, and applying it left exactly one faction in the world able to muster. Structural eligibility gates the spawn roll rather than the reverse, after a roll-first sweep spent its whole probability budget on barren guilds and produced zero bands. Bands are named for whose they are ("The Arcane Circle's Ravens"), not where they met.
✅ THR-731 (PR 2, opposed group resolution) — a company that walks into a band now fights it. The pairing rides identity, not template lists: a completing company encounter whose hex holds a foreign band gets a synthesized band counter-action (`bandRole` → `encounter.band_defend` / `band_raid`), and `detectContestations` gains a group pass that emits the pair with the initiator attacking and the band defending — bands answer, they never open, so no scale/FIFO tiebreak is needed. The group pass runs first and *claims*, which deliberately gives an authored `contestsWith` contest the stronger hold on any action it wants. Resolution stayed where it was: `resolveContestationPair` (TB-044) does the rolling, extended only so each side prices its step through `resolveGroupStep` — a six-strong band used to fight exactly as hard as its leader alone, the one place in the engine where company strength silently did not apply. Two substrate finds, both grep-verified: `opposingGroupId` was named by THR-74's plan and never implemented (zero hits), so this PR adds it rather than populating it; and `contested_won`/`contested_lost` had shipped with TB-044 carrying ChapterView display strings, a `playerReceipts` severity mapping and an `isActionSuccess` branch, with **zero producers** — group contests are its first, so losing a fight finally reads differently from failing one. Consequences beyond the step's own ops: cohesion ±, a casualty on a decisive loss (marked deceased, never the leader while anyone else stands, so `reconcileLostMembers` closes the edge next tick and the shipped cascade can carry the loser to dissolution), and a mutual `hostile_to` grudge carrying its tick and cause. The band counter-templates are ordinary group-exclusive encounters rather than a synth-only pool — fencing them off would have been exactly the special-casing this ticket is under orders to resist, and would have left them unreachable in a live run. Proven organically, no forcing: at t81 (seed 42, medium) Company of the Inn met the Temple of the Spheres' Sparrows, killed Bagaabraa and took the ground; Flintlock's Band met the same span at t84; the band fell 0.70 → 0.19 and disbanded.
✅ THR-731 (PR 3, confrontation content) — the fight got a face, and a reachability hole closed on the way. Four authored group-exclusive confrontations — **The Ambush**, **Den Assault**, **The Guild Falls**, **The Standoff** — each gated on a live opponent by a new `requiresOpposingBand` template flag, because an encounter *about* fighting a particular band is a scene with an empty chair in it when no band is there. Reaches rotate across every template's steps so best-member substitution spotlights a different companion each step rather than the same fighter three times; all four score 100/100 on the prose scorer with zero flags. Enforcing the gate surfaced the finding worth more than the content: company templates travel **two** draw paths and only one gated. `generateUnifiedCandidates` has checked `minGroupMembers` since THR-74, but the location-cache path (`getEncountersByLocationType` → `encounterCache` → `encounterFilterPipeline`) had **no actor-affinity stage whatsoever** — measured at implementation time, `getEncountersByLocationType("ruins")` returned 7 group-exclusive templates, including THR-74's own shipped `sunken_vault`/`broken_span`/`hollow_watch`, with nothing downstream reading `actorAffinities`. Party-exclusive delves were reachable by solo agents in direct contradiction of the authoring contract written in their own source comment. Stage 3 — the pipeline's documented prerequisites stage, previously a "placeholder for future trait prerequisites" — now enforces `minGroupMembers` and `requiresOpposingBand`, both resolved lazily at most once per agent. The Standoff's non-lethal rung is made structural rather than left to a low roll: a `contestNonLethal` flag skips the casualty roll entirely, so losing costs cohesion, standing and the ground but never a life, and an unknown template id defaults to lethal so a missing lookup cannot silently make band conflict bloodless. `PendingEncounterSeed.opposingGroupId` shipped in PR 2 with **zero readers** — a seed naming its enemy dropped it in silence — so the seed → action carry now re-validates at spawn (node exists ∧ `isBandNode` ∧ active ∧ ≥1 living member) and degrades to an ordinary encounter rather than pointing at a corpse. **Not yet observed firing organically:** contests keep firing on their own (t85, seed 42 medium), but no confrontation drew in runs to 250 ticks — the family needs company ∧ live foreign band ∧ matching location subtype ∧ winning the scoring pass simultaneously, and bands and companies are rarely colocated *at a matching subtype* on this seed. Reachability is unit-proven at both gates; deterministic live proof waits on PR 4's `spawn band`, which the plan's Done-when already anticipates.
✅ THR-731 (PR 4, band CLI + Rivals line — ticket complete) — the two observability gaps closed, and with them a defect that had been hiding behind them. `spawn band <faction> [--role raider|defender]` reaches all three surfaces (headless CLI, in-game CLI, `__DEBUG.spawnBand`) and forces a muster while keeping **every** structural precondition — per-faction cap, member reserve, colocated cluster, monster-faction skip — with each refusal naming the precondition that failed, because "why is this guild not mustering?" is the real question. Deliberately **no `--hex`** despite the plan mirroring `spawn npc`: a band musters from its faction's own colocated members, so a hex would either be ignored or mean teleporting a muster into being, the one thing the shipped spawner refuses. It is currently the only way a `raider` band exists at all (THR-767 owes that role a population). The Company section gained a prose **Rivals** line — `agentDetail` reads `hostile_to` off the company node in *both* directions and dedupes the mutual pair the contest writes, rendering "There is blood between them and The Errant Keys of The Arcane Circle": never a count, never the `since` tick, and absent entirely for a company that has never fought. **PR 3's predicted suspect was correct.** `encounter.confront_guild_falls` and `encounter.band_defend` both gated on `sublocation-type.guildhall`; worldgen mints `sublocation-type.guild-hall` — 34 on seed 42 medium, and zero of the unhyphenated id on any seed. One missing hyphen made the ticket's own capstone and the band's counter-encounter **unreachable by construction**, with a green suite throughout. Now locked by a derived content-integrity test whose two design choices are both load-bearing: the mintable set is computed from the five sources that actually mint sublocations (never hand-listed, so it cannot drift from the generators), and it reads the merged `locationSubtypes` rather than the authored `sublocationTypes` — because `toUnifiedTemplate` folds the latter into the former, so a check on the authored field matches nothing and passes vacuously. The first draft did exactly that and "passed" with the bug reintroduced; the shipped version fails on the typo, on nothing else, and asserts against its own vacuity. Done-when #4 demonstrated headlessly: a company relocated into a Great Silverhold guild hall resolved The Guild Falls against a colocated Arcane Circle defender band — outcomes [failure, success, success], company cohesion 0.54 → 0.70, band 0.70 → 0.46, mutual grudges written at t61. **Honest negative, kept in canon rather than dropped:** the family is now gate-reachable (all four assert against `generateUnifiedCandidates` with a real band present) and the loop is proven, but no confrontation was observed winning a scoring pass unforced — a company parked beside two foreign bands drew 7 other encounters over 100 ticks. That is a base-rate/tuning question, not a wiring one, and the rulebook says so rather than implying the family fires on its own.
✅ THR-732 (Reunite + Sunder — the company arc closes) — the god's two remaining company verbs, completing the triangle Draw Together and Bless left open: one that reaches backward, one that breaks. **Reunite** is cast on a company that has *already ended* — the only card in the game whose target is a piece of history. It opens a `reuniteUntilTick` window on the dead node and stamps **Draw Together's own** `convergePullHexCol/_HexRow/_UntilTick` triple on every gatherable former member, so the scattered bend their own roads homeward through `computeConvergenceBonus` and no second convergence mechanism exists to drift; a `REUNITE_COMPAT_BONUS` lets two old comrades clear the formation threshold on shared history alone, and the re-formed company takes a variant of the old name (*The Quiet Wardens, Re-formed*) under a new `reunite` formation cause that deliberately outranks `draw_together` in precedence — judged on the pull alone every reunion would have been told as an ordinary divine gathering. Both endings are authored: **The Reunion** when they find each other, **The Road Not Taken** when the window lapses unanswered, because a god who calls and is not answered is the premise working, not a failure to hide. **Sunder** is Bless's exact mirror — same target class, same window shape, every read amplifying where Bless suppresses: dissent bites ×2 (`groupCohesion`), a fraying company's members leave ×2 as readily (`groupDissolution`), and the fray drama pool treats the company as frayed whatever the number says (`phaseGroups`), so the visible output is scenes rather than a falling gauge. The two windows **do not cancel** — both may be open at once, each read independently, and the tug-of-war is left unresolved by design. **The finding that would have made Reunite inert:** the plan named its input as the disbanded company's `roster`, and verified that property exists and is persisted — but `dissolveGroup` sets `roster: []` on the way out, so a faithful implementation finds zero gatherable members forever, silently, on exactly the input the verb takes. What survives dissolution is the `member_of` edges it stamps with `leftAtTick`, which `groupDissolution.ts`'s own header calls the historical record; `getFormerGroupMembers` walks those, and the shipped test asserts `roster === []` and the edge-walk returning all three riders in the same body, so a roster-based implementation fails the test that documents why. Also caught: `sphereAffinity: 'dusk'` — a word borrowed from a neighbouring content pool whose keys turn out not to be sphere ids at all (6 of 8 are unreachable; filed THR-770) — which crashed the milestone-beat render sweep and is now `entropy`, the sphere `reach: 'shadow'` actually maps to. Both verbs are breadth unlocks granted together by *An Empty Road*, the milestone that fires the first time a company the player was bound to comes apart — which is Reunite's own precondition, so neither card arrives before the world holds something for it to act on. Three interface rows 🟢 LIVE, the convergence one falsified during authoring (renaming the written key fails the guard). Card art deferred to THR-769: none of the four company verbs has art, including the two THR-74 shipped.
✅ THR-734 (UL: group-layer terms) — the group layer finally has canonical words. Five entries into the Agents shard: **Group** (the engine object — `actorType: 'group'` + `groupType`, no `located_at` edge because position derives from the leader, and `armyState` absent is what separates it from an army sharing the same actorType), **Company** (the player-facing word; "party" survives only as an internal `groupType` value and must never reach prose or UI), **Group Cohesion** (event-driven 0–1 rendered as bound/holding/frayed/breaking, never as a number outside the DebugPanel), **Draw Together** and **Bless this Company**. The handoff's instruction to mark the two verbs not-yet-implemented was reversed against the code: THR-74 PR 2b has since landed and all four `company.*` verbs are live UATs, so entries claiming design-only status would have written drift into the artifact that exists to prevent it — the handoff's own governing clause said "reconciled against shipped code". Every constant, threshold and symbol cited was grep-verified before it was written down. Filed on the way: THR-771 (`GROUP_DISSOLUTION_THRESHOLD`'s doc comment has the two lower cohesion bands swapped relative to `getCohesionState`).
✅ THR-737 (trait_grant consumers — the leak one layer up, closed) — `trait_grant` was the textbook write-only contract: 22 authored payloads across five catalogs, a correct resolver collecting `grantedTraits`, and **zero production readers**. `hasGrantedTrait` was called only by its own definition, a re-export, and tests, so an item advertising `intimidate` conferred nothing a mortal, an encounter, or a spell could act on. THR-722 had retired the parallel `possesses`-edge `grants[]` property for exactly this reason and migrated its payload onto `effects[]` — which moved the leak rather than closing it, and the interface row said so in as many words. Closed by a `collectGrantedTraits` aggregate wrapping `hasGrantedTrait`, consumed by the three production gates that ask "does this agent have capability X?": encounter eligibility in `filterByPrerequisites`, spell prerequisites in `checkPrerequisites`, and ambition eligibility via `buildAmbitionAgentSnapshot` plus the parallel `worldSeed` initial-assignment path. **The ticket's own suggested read site would have shipped a vacuous gate.** It cites `encounterScoring.ts:376` (`grantsTraitWhileHeld` → `ruin_seeker`) as the precedent shape, and wiring the aggregate there types cleanly, tests green, and changes nothing — because not one of the 22 `trait_grant` payloads grants `ruin_seeker`. The enumeration that mattered was of the *granted* values against the *required* ones: `master_smith` appears on both sides (The Worldforge Anvil grants it; `ambition_forge_legend` gates on it), and that intersection is now asserted directly, so re-authoring either side fails the suite instead of silently re-emptying the gate. `blockedByTraits` was wired alongside `requiredTraits` for symmetry — a grant that can unlock scarred-gated content while leaving scarred-*blocked* content open is half a gate. Granted traits carry no level, so they satisfy level-bearing requirements at `GRANTED_TRAIT_EFFECTIVE_LEVEL` (1), matching the `grantedTraitLevel ?? 1` default the sibling possession path already uses; the aggregate is fail-soft and lazily cached per agent, since the encounter pipeline runs for every agent every tick. Contract `attachment-trait-grant-effects` 🔴 LEAKED → 🟢 LIVE with dated evidence. Live proof it is reachable in a normal run, not just in tests: seed 42 / medium at tick 30 carries 2 agents holding 3 granted traits (`cavalry_charge`, `rapid_retreat`, `intimidate`) from starter attachments — grants that, until this change, every gate in the game ignored.
✅ THR-754 (Browser-verify: sanctioned evidence routes) — the DoD's 1920×1080 screenshot clause was called "binary" while the unattended lane could satisfy it by no route at all: the Browser pane refuses to composite with no pane displayed, Playwright's capture returned its own dimensions regardless of `browser_resize`, and a bare `filename` wrote the PNG outside the repo. Five recurrences each rediscovered a different workaround. The clause stays binary; it now carries a ladder naming which capture discharges it per lane and surface — attended unchanged, unattended via Playwright MCP with an **absolute** `filename` inside the session worktree, portal-rendered overlays proven by accessibility-tree capture (CDP omits the portal layer entirely, on shipped surfaces too), and a capture whose real size differs from 1920×1080 stating its actual dimensions and discharging the viewport contract by DOM assertion from the Browser pane. Deviations are declared as `Browser-verify substitution: <route> — <reason>`, mirroring `Browser-verify exempt:`. Answers impediment #199's durable-fix line and decides the THR-696 retro question in favour of naming the split. Requirement 1 also stopped naming `preview_resize`/`preview_screenshot`, which no longer exist.
✅ THR-755 (gate-credibility sweep) — six rows, one shape: a gate whose output contradicts its verdict. `lint:plan-doc`'s scoping had already been fixed upstream (THR-686/692), leaving a subtler defect — a *waived* doc and a *mistyped path* printed the identical `skipped (no candidate files found)`, so the exemptions that fix was made of could not be verified from the gate's own output; it now names every waived doc. `check:wiki-freshness:blocking` printed `FAIL` plus the full remediation text and only afterwards discovered the `Wiki-freshness-exempt:` token and exited 0, so the last thing a reader saw was a failure and a to-do already satisfied; the exemption is now resolved before any verdict prints, a hard-wrapped reason is joined across continuation lines instead of being truncated mid-sentence (the audited half of the escape hatch, and what `weekly-project-hygiene` reviews), and blocking mode asserts `is stale` rather than hedging `may be stale` about a claim it is about to exit 1 over. `check:process`'s `deferred-ref` rule flagged the drift scanner's own report template forever, since that template renders a row labelled with the marker it counts. The interface-map generator's `nothing produces this contract` / `the consumer is starving` verdicts now name the cheaper second cause — a mis-declared `mechanism.symbols` — with the literal grep to run. And `social-encounter-content.ts` carried a duplicate `import type { UnifiedActionTemplate }` at line 2462 that was a hard PARSE_ERROR for vite-node. **The row-3 fix reproduced row 3 on its first run:** the comment written to explain the exclusion quoted the marker literally, and the gate reported two fresh false errors on those exact lines — a marker lint cannot tell a marker from a mention of one, the same vector THR-738 closed for `Fixes THR-XX`. That also decided the ticket's open question in favour of path-scoping over literal-detection, since the explanatory comment would have been *code* rather than a literal and would have failed either way. Guard falsified before trusting it (a probe under `src/` still flagged, one under `scripts/drift-scan/` not). Typecheck 3519 → 3517; baseline refreshed.
✅ THR-786 (traits trigger unification — one predicate, six sites) — the six trait-predicate vocabularies (encounter filter pipeline, effect-predicate `has_trait:` sugar, `graphConditions`, ambition snapshot eligibility, spell prerequisites, item-granted keys) now resolve through one `collectBearerTraitRefs`/`bearerMatchesPredicate` on ANY-match across four ref forms (node id, short id, display name, tag), with `resolveTraitPredicate` as the bearer-agnostic entry point and a `SimulationRuntime`-owned `TraitRefIndex` for content sweeps. Unchanged-behavior contract suite written first as the kill criterion: 31 PRESERVED assertions green pre- and post-migration, 6 labelled widening/repair cases each verified failing beforehand. New `__DEBUG.validateTraitRefs()` sweeps all six authored surfaces and reported the finding that outgrew the ticket — 62 authored trait gates resolve to no trait definition (THR-800), because authored refs are bare snake_case while every definition uses `trait.<category>.<kebab>` ids / Title Case names / `#tags`; masked all this time by the self-closing grant-key path. Two dead display-name reads repaired in passing; template gate fields still undeclared (THR-801). Predicate-only floor — no minting, tick phases, PRNG, or new node/edge types.
✅ THR-801 (template trait-gate fields declared — the phantom API made real) — `filterByPrerequisites` had read `template.requiredTraits`/`blockedByTraits` every tick since THR-773, but neither field was declared on `UnifiedActionTemplate`: a gate evaluated by the engine and authorable by nobody, where any template that tried to declare one simply failed to typecheck. Two additive optional fields (`readonly requiredTraits?: readonly TraitPredicate[]`, `readonly blockedByTraits?: readonly string[]` — the asymmetry deliberate, since holding a blocking trait at any level blocks) cleared **13** baseline errors, 3517 → 3504, with **zero net-new**, proven by diffing the full `tsc -b` error set either side of the change rather than trusting the count. Both halves of the ticket's "two errors in one file" prediction were low: 8 sat in `encounterFilterPipeline.ts` (six TS2339 plus the TS7006 implicit-any cascades they caused) and the other 5 in a **second production reader nobody had identified** — `src/engine/kpi/branchingDistance.ts`, the diagnostic reporting how many agents a gate excludes — which THR-786's migration could not see because its reads sat inside the red baseline (THR-489) as "property does not exist"; it still compares refs by raw node id instead of the shared ANY-match resolver, latent while no gate is authored (THR-802). Authoring deferred to THR-778 (WS5) under the Done-when's stated alternative, because THR-800 had just shown all 62 authored trait refs to be dead — minting a gate now would author the 63rd and pre-empt the vocabulary THR-788 is still settling. The regression guard is type-level with the ratchet as its teeth, not vitest: the existing site-1 cases mock `getAnyEncounterById` with untyped literals and pass whether the interface declares the fields or not, which is precisely how the gap survived two shipping tickets.
✅ THR-797 (reaper no longer reaps live sessions) — the hourly `clean-stale-git.sh` judged liveness only by git-admin-dir mtime, which stops moving during a closeout that is still writing Linear/doc/impediment files; at the 08:40 run on 2026-07-26 it removed a worktree ~5h after that session's merge, and because `.claude/worktrees/<name>` lives inside the home tree's working copy, the session's next `git checkout -b` silently landed on the home tree. `is_live` now also probes working-tree file mtimes (the same signal the orphan sweep already trusted — that sweep called the very same path "recent activity" two lines after the removal WARN in that one run), a 90-minute `WORKTREE_MERGE_GRACE_MINUTES` hold covers the narrower post-merge case, and the branch pass keeps any branch whose unregistered worktree corpse is still active, closing the THR-673 chain that deleted the branch an hour later.
✅ THR-803 (encounter chains work for the first time) — `recordChainStageCompletion` had zero production callers, so `agent.properties.chainProgress` was read by four modules and written by none; and `ENCOUNTER_CHAINS` named stages as bare keys (`knowledge_test`) while every real template is `encounter.knowledge_test`, so `templateToChains` never matched and the gate returned `true` for all nine stages. The subsystem was inert, not gating — the filed symptom ("6 of 9 stages permanently undrawable") was the inverse of the truth, the same never-intersecting-vocabularies shape as THR-800. Stage ids repointed to live template ids and guarded by a test resolving each through `getAnyEncounterById`; `applyChainStageCompletion` wired into `executeStepResult` (the resolution site that owns graph writes, gated on the whole encounter landing rather than a step passing), persisting progress in place, granting `CHAIN_COMPLETION_CAPABILITY_BONUS` once via an idempotent `chain_mastery_*` trait, touching `worldVersion`, and emitting one aggregate `chain_progress` trace per advance. Verified live at tick 150 of seed-42 medium: five agents with written progress, two at stage 1. Guild rank gating deferred to THR-805 — chains may be the wrong mechanism (rank is already first-class on `member_of`, `faction_rank:` predicate exists), a chain stage holds one template id where each guild tier holds several, and `MAX_ACTIVE_CHAINS=2` would make it a balance change.
✅ THR-805 (guild rank gating — the senior/elite tail finally asks for standing) — the mechanism choice THR-803 deferred, resolved against **both** candidates it named. `EncounterChain` loses on shape (a stage holds one template id; a guild tier holds several) and on balance (`MAX_ACTIVE_CHAINS = 2`). The `faction_rank:` predicate loses outright as a **dead gate**: it reads `agentNode.properties.factionRank`, which nothing in the codebase writes, so `ctx.factionRank` is permanently 0 — wiring it would have been THR-803's own defect in a new costume, precisely as that ticket warned. The mechanism that won was already in the data and simply unread: `FACTION_ENCOUNTER_META.minRank` names a required rank tier **per template** across ~150 metas, so it matches the tier-holds-several shape exactly and cannot drift the way the tiers' `encounterAccess` prefix lists already have (`merchant_consortium` declares `mc_trade.*` against `mct.*` templates, so a prefix gate would fail closed for that guild). `meetsFactionRankRequirement` derives rank from `reputation` on every check rather than trusting the edge's cached `rank`/`role`, which refresh only when a tier boundary is crossed; non-membership closes the gate as the one deliberately non-fail-soft negative, and unresolvable data fails **open** so a typo cannot orphan content. Gating is scoped by authored `questType`, not by `minRank`'s presence — `minRank` is required, so presence-gating would have shut all 123 `standard` quest/social templates behind membership and violated the Done-when. The first implementation fired on nothing: guarded on `template &&` like its five neighbours, while `getAnyEncounterById` cannot resolve any cache-registered regional template — which means the broken, group-exclusive, confrontation, trait and blocked-by-trait gates are all inert for those same ids (**THR-811**, High). Of 60 rank-gated metas only **12** are cache-reachable — exactly the guild tail THR-779/THR-803 rescued — and **6 of those sit behind a 0.85 reputation floor the economy never reaches past ~tick 100** (**THR-810**). Proven in both directions on a live seed-42 world, and falsified by disabling the gate (2 of 14 red, both closed-direction).
✅ THR-811 (five prerequisite gates could not see the template they gate on) — `filterByPrerequisites` resolved its template with `getAnyEncounterById`, which covers only the encounter pools, so **43 of the 213 template ids the encounter cache can register** came back `undefined` and every `template?.` gate — broken, group-exclusive, confrontation, `requiredTraits`, `blockedByTraits` — fell straight through and passed them unchecked. Running the membership predicate instead of trusting where THR-805 found it more than doubled the set: not just the 17 `CACHE_REGISTERED_REGIONAL_TEMPLATES` guild ids but the branching quest families (`enc.*`, `crafting.quest.*`, `liminal.quest.*`) and the whole `reputation.*` / sphere-themed set-piece tier. Fixed once at the lookup (`getUnifiedTemplateById`, 0 of 213 unresolvable) rather than five times at the gates. The ticket's cost warning was real — the superset lookup measured 4× slower on a per-entry-per-agent-per-tick path — and a lazily-built id Map inverted it to **4.3× faster than the status quo** (18 ns vs 78 ns over 30,968 live entries); lazy because the module sits in an import cycle with the engine, module-scope because both source arrays are immutable after init. Checking object *identity* rather than mere definedness caught what the "strict superset" argument missed: for 39 ids both lookups resolve to **different objects**, `UNIFIED_ACTION_TEMPLATES` holding the `withGroupAffinity`-swept copy against the pool's pre-sweep original, so the pipeline had been reading the unswept one. Benign and shown so — the objects differ only in `actorAffinities`, the sweep only appends, and **0** ids change group-exclusivity verdict — after the first version of that assertion was reframed from "no cache template is group-exclusive" (which correctly failed on THR-731's authored band set) to "none *became*". Gate firing proven per gate on a real previously-unresolvable template via restoring in-place field sets, since no shipped encounter template declares these fields at all; falsified against the old lookup at 3 of 15 red. The broken gate is excluded from that proof rather than faked: `BROKEN_GATE_ENABLED` ships false. A 60-tick seed-42 A/B run is byte-identical, so nothing became unreachable — this widens what the gates can see, and THR-808 is the authoring that will use it.
✅ THR-808 (the dynasty founder's death now ends the dynasty) — `ambition_found_dynasty` gated its only abandonment trigger on a trait named `living` that no producer has ever minted, so the ambition had no reachable abandonment path: once assigned it ran until completed, whether or not the founder was alive. Aliveness is engine state, not a trait — `properties.deceased` has three writers and five readers — so the trigger became a new `agent_deceased` `GraphCondition` reading it directly, with a shared `isDeceased` helper that deliberately rejects the two never-written spellings beside it (`eliminated`, `status: 'dead'`). Verified `phaseAmbitionProgress` does not filter deceased actors, so the condition genuinely fires. The ticket's other class-2 member, `rare_ore_secured`, was reclassified rather than implemented: `'resource'` is declared in `NodeType` but no `resource` node is ever constructed, so a variant there would have read state nothing writes. Dead-ref ratchet 22 → 21; residue tracked as THR-813, adjacent `target_agent_eliminated` defect as THR-812.
✅ THR-809 (condition + mastery trait definitions are seeded at last, so a lost brawl marks somebody) — `MASTERY_TRAIT_DEFINITIONS` + `CONDITION_TRAIT_DEFINITIONS` reached the graph through exactly one path, `phaseEncounterTraits.ensureTraitNodes`, called from inside the orchestrator's loop over the legacy `state.encounterProgress` collection that the unified-action pipeline no longer populates. The loop body never ran, so 13 definition nodes were never inserted and every `condition_attachment` / `apply_condition` effect naming a definition-file condition took the `template_missing` fail-soft branch and silently no-opped — THR-783 wired `failureMetadata.effects` correctly and still could not show a wound landing. The verdict recorded is **init-time, not resolver-lazy**: a new `seedEncounterTraitDefinitions` runs from `seedWorld`, making definition presence an invariant of every world graph rather than a race against whichever system fires first, and removing the need for a presence check at the resolution site. The sweep the ticket asked for is what changed the fix's shape: **four** `ensure*TraitNodes` helpers short-circuited on `DEFINITIONS[0]` — "if the first exists they all do" — so any foreign path minting that one id permanently skipped the remainder, which is precisely how the 1 condition + 2 mastery nodes previously in the graph (all from `ECONOMIC_TRAIT_DEFINITIONS`, whose seeder always had the correct per-node shape) coexisted with 13 missing ones. All four are now per-node; the three siblings (reputation 17, core 10, personality 16 — each measured complete at tick 5) were latent rather than live, and fixing them is a deliberate widening beyond the ticket's one-guard wording, named as such. - ✅ **THR-1030** (2026-08-08) — `?outcome=<band>` makes any authored ending reachable from a URL, and reports when it did not get you there. The director asked to test all the different aftermaths and no lever existed: `?spawn=` stages an encounter, `?testavatar` balances the actor, but the band is rolled at resolution, and on a balanced avatar the tails are the *rare* bands by design — so the endings most needing review were the hardest to reach. Of the ticket's two shapes, **force the band** was taken over **enumerate the variants** for the reason the ticket gave: the failure this must catch is "this authored band is unreachable", and only a real resolution proves reachability — a preview renders the authored model and calls a band fine whether or not anything can produce it. Scoped to one `templateId` — a global pin would force every agent's every step and make the reviewed ending unrepresentative — and it reaches the two auto-success early returns too, or a failure asked for on a divine action would come back a silent success. **The anti-vacuity half is the deliverable:** a pinned band nobody authored would render the *base* ending under the band's name, laundering the exact defect THR-989 and THR-973 exist to find, so every pinned resolution records a verdict — `band_rendered` only when the band is authored *and* the action landed on it, `unauthored_band` when it does not exist, `outcome_diverged` when the action aggregated the pinned steps elsewhere (a pinned `near_miss` always does, having no `UnifiedActionOutcome` counterpart; a pinned `failure` does unless `failBehavior` is `fail_action`) — each warning to console and readable via `__DEBUG.getOutcomePinVerdict()`. - ✅ **THR-1038** (2026-08-08) — 15 mercenary-company templates carried an aftermath in a schema nothing reads, and the red baseline is what hid it. Their `aftermathConfig` was not a `BranchAwareAftermathConfig` at all — no `branchOnStep`, no `variants`, no `fallback`, just a bare `reactions` array — so `resolveAftermathVariant` fell through to an `undefined` fallback and `applyAftermathOutcomeBand` read `byOutcome` off it, throwing on **every** resolved action; the tick loop's fail-soft envelope swallowed it, so nothing was red and the authored aftermath on all 15 reached nobody. The ticket's last Done-when — eyeball the endings via `?spawn=&outcome=` — **could not be met**: every `mc.*` template crashes the encounter stage first, `buildUnifiedEncounterStageModel` reading `narrativeTemplates.initiation` unguarded on templates that declare no `narrativeTemplates`. Attributed rather than assumed — it reproduces identically on the pre-change tree — and filed as THR-1040. These endings resolve correctly at the engine level and stay invisible in the UI until that lands; two silent-death layers on the same templates, this ticket removed the inner one.
- ✅ **THR-1042** (2026-08-08) — an authored ending overrides the prose; it no longer erases the facts. One line in `buildAftermath` decided what the player is told changed — `authoredVariant?.changes ?? summary.changes` — which reads as *if an author wrote an ending, show only what the author listed*. Every engine-derived change was dropped the moment a template carried an `aftermathConfig`: a prize the reward pool actually rolled and granted, a capability that grew, a reputation that moved. The world changed and the ending did not say so. The original intent was defensible when written — the comment above it said it was suppressing "raw mechanical deltas" in favour of curated content — but it suppressed the **facts** to get rid of the **presentation**, and those two had already been separated elsewhere: `engine/aftermathWords.ts` bands derived deltas into English long before they reach this surface, so the suppression was solving a problem that no longer existed at the cost of the one thing the aftermath is for. It was also a hard blocker on re-adopting `rewardPool` in new-era encounters, the two features being mutually exclusive by construction. **The thing worth knowing before touching it was that the engine had already done the merge:** `unifiedActionResolution.ts:2418` assembles the summary as `[...derived, ...authored]`, so the surface was never missing data — it was re-resolving the authored variant itself and throwing away the half it had not asked for, which reframes the fix from "go fetch the derived changes" to "stop discarding them". `mergeAftermathChanges` replaces the `??`: authored changes lead, derived facts follow, identical ids collapse so the engine's own merge is not double-counted **and** a summary that never went through it still gains the authored half rather than losing it, and a derived change is suppressed only when an authored one declares the same THR-1004 `concepts` — never English prose-matching, since two sentences can state one fact in different words and substring matching would both miss those and collide on unrelated changes sharing a phrase. Authored changes normally carry no `concepts` at all, so the de-duplication fires rarely, and that is the design rather than a gap: stating a fact twice is recoverable, hiding it is the defect (NFP #4). Falsified before trusted — with the merge reverted, exactly the 2 prize-survival assertions fail while the 2 guarding the merge's own correctness pass, which is why both halves are kept. Browser-verified at 1920×1080 on `enc.letters_of_introduction`, the one shipped template carrying both an `aftermathConfig` and a rolling `rewardPool`: **9 consequence chips where the pre-fix build showed 4**, the four recovered ones reading "Vara's Gold grew a little", "Vara's reputation for Gold deepened again", "Vara's Gold grew sharply", "Vara's reputation for Gold deepened further" — magnitudes in words, concepts carrying tooltip and link. Reported honestly: the `?outcome=success` pin returned `unauthored_band` because that template authors no bands, which is orthogonal to this fix, and the `aftermathConfig` path was genuinely exercised since all four authored chips resolved from the formal-channel branch variant. Two pre-existing Law-14 violations found on the surface *as composed* and filed rather than folded in — THR-1050 (reaction `label`/`intent` bypass `enrichProse`, so `{cast:patron}` reaches the player verbatim; 32 lines across 6 files) and THR-1051 (authored prose says "The content_grant fires", naming an effect-kind enum to the player). - ✅ **THR-1044** (2026-08-08) — the `encounter.*` family can bind cast at all. Every nudge-era encounter reached the stage with no cast, and not for want of authoring: `withDefaultSupportBundle` keys on the template-id prefix, `encounter.*` had no entry, and **0 of its 191 templates declared a `supportBundle` of their own** — so `{cast:*}` placeholders in that family had nothing to resolve against by construction, upstream of anything a content author could have written. Bind-only throughout: every spec stays `pre-seeded`, so a default attaches an NPC already standing at the anchor or stays unresolved, and zero world population is added. One pre-existing test needed a real fix rather than an update: `prerequisiteTemplateResolution` asserts the pool lookup and the unified lookup differ only by the transforms registry assembly applies, and it named just one of the two — `actorAffinities` — because `supportBundle` had never before landed on a template that also lives in an encounter pool, so the omission was invisible until now. 973 files / 15367 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3462, build clean, 30-tick smoke at 383 agents.

- ✅ **THR-1068** (2026-08-10) — `autoResolveTick` gets the consumer it never had. The deadline had been stamped on every `auto_resolve` notification since TB-035 and read back by nobody: five production readers, every one treating it as a flag or a label. The ticket filed the fork as *"a design call, not only a repair"* — expire or queue — and it resolved as a **technical verdict**, because the intent is already recorded in four places that all agree: the mode is named `auto_resolve`, `RETINUE_VIGNETTE_TIMEOUT` is documented "Ticks before retinue vignette auto-resolves", `autoResolveTick` is "Tick when auto-resolve fires", and THR-880's own comment describes the alternative as "silently auto-resolving after RETINUE_VIGNETTE_TIMEOUT ticks". Nothing anywhere describes queueing. The ticket's second worry — that expiry must "resolve through the normal path so consequences fire, not just flip a flag" — dissolves on inspection: a notification is a player-facing record, never the mechanism by which an encounter resolves, and every pre-existing resolve site writes that same single flag and mutates nothing else. **Two exemptions, both deliberate and both test-pinned so a later completeness sweep cannot read them as oversights.** Aftermath is exempt because at this tier the badge is the player's only route into a concluded beat (THR-943), so expiring the conclusion record 8 ticks after it appears would delete the only surface reporting what happened — narrative loss at the tier that opted out of interrupts precisely so outcomes would be *reported*; those records still leave via the 50-tick trim, and they keep a non-null deadline because that field also carries "do not auto-open", which nulling would make every aftermath interrupt at the one tier that must never be. Legacy-sourced steps are exempt because the dedup key set drops resolved legacy records by design, so retiring one while its `encounterProgress` is active would re-emit it next tick forever — filed as THR-1069, which asks reachability first, since if the legacy pipeline no longer produces threaded notifications the answer is to delete the branch rather than fix it. **Two corrections to the ticket's own account:** "accumulates forever" is imprecise — the orchestrator has always trimmed at 50 ticks, so the pile was bounded at six times the authored deadline rather than unbounded; and the backlog also cost per-tick work, since `phaseAscendantHandFilter` runs template adaptation plus a forecast per unresolved record every tick. **Evidenced headlessly, and the reason matters:** the live route could not produce the population — the seeded First generated no encounter across 120 driven ticks, and `__DEBUG.inspectEncounterPipeline` reads a snapshot that lags `__DEBUG.tick()` (reporting `tick: 0` at engine tick 120), so a browser reading of "zero overdue" would have been an empty-population pass wearing a verdict's clothes (impediment #521). The wiring is instead pinned by an integration test driving `runTick` with the exact measured shape — three notifications 32/36/37 ticks overdue at tick 113 — asserting the overdue count returns to zero, the exempt records survive a real tick, and a future deadline is untouched, that last one guarding against a "fix" that drains the badge by retiring everything in sight. The veil's countdown is clamped and reads "auto-resolving now" rather than `in 0 ticks`. A pre-existing Law 13 violation on the same strip — `auto-resolves in 4 ticks`, a raw numeral needing a duration word scale that does not yet exist — was filed as THR-1070 rather than silently invented. One gate earned its keep: the new trace category was unregistered, so `trace-vocabulary.test.ts` failed and prevented a trace that would have been emitted faithfully and been invisible in the DebugPanel. 981 files / 15,510 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3451, build clean, smoke reached tick 30 with 383 agents.

Showing mercy makes you more ruthless, everywhere except stone. A second independent half rides with it: the `test` blocks bind pole letters to the *choices* while the engine binds them to the *profile*, so on those same 37 the formative path and the legacy path write opposite directions for one narrative outcome, invisibly from either side. A uniform flip — the obvious reading of "fix the 37" — would have broken the one reach that was right while leaving its cross-path disagreement in place. **Scope closed by measurement, not assumption:** only 45 templates carry `axiologicalShifts` at all and 40 are exactly the converted set, **zero** have shifts without a `test`, and the 122 `reach_specific`/`domain_specific`/`general` templates carry none — which also retires THR-1064's parting concern about `RC-STONE-01…05`, since they have neither a shift nor a target pair. The remaining five are `AX-META-01…05`, outside Batch A by construction and left unfiled per the 2026-08-10 throttle. The guard (`axiologicalPolarity.test.ts`, 202 assertions) rests on **one** hand-recorded table — which choice is the first pole, a reading of prose no derivation can establish and which would be circular if taken from the shift signs — and derives the rest: clean bands match their choice by content-word overlap at a **≥35% margin** across all 40. `brokenInto*` bands are deliberately excluded and the reason is a property of the content — they narrate a *crossing*, opening on one pole and ending at the other, so they carry both choices' vocabulary and score 26/40 and 20/40. **Falsified rather than merely green:** run against the pre-fix library it fails on 40 distinct templates with zero overlap, 35 legacy-path and 5 formative-path, the 5 being exactly the stone set. 992 files / 15,885 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3447, build clean, smoke to tick 30 with 383 agents. - ✅ **THR-998** (2026-08-12) — the focused action card stopped claiming odds it cannot deliver. `riskHintLine(maxStepDifficulty)` bucketed the **authored** step difficulty, but `applyScaleDifficultyAdjust` caps difficulty at `capability − MIN_PROBABILITY_BY_SCALE[scale]`, which for a fresh god is **0** at `personal` and `local` — **85% of the actor-target slot list** — so two cards priced 0.20 and 0.50 read *"A steady working."* and *"A perilous working."* while resolving to the identical probability. **Christian delegated the direction pick** (chat 2026-08-12, canon `process.md` rule 4); the sacred outcome he set was *the card never claims odds that are not real*. **Direction 1 was implemented far enough to measure and rejected**: bucketing the same three words on resolved probability is truthful but collapses 85% of the slot list onto one word (P = 0.70 personal / 0.65 local), and one word swallowing the card face is the exact failure the risk line was introduced to prevent — `playerCastBalance.test.ts` bounds any word at 60%. **Shipped direction 2**: the line is a function of `effectiveCastDifficulty` alone — the difficulty surviving offset and floor — so **two casts with equal odds read the same line by construction, not by measurement**, and where the floor capped the price away the card names the working's *size* instead, because at that scale reach genuinely *is* the term setting the odds. **Self-maintaining**: the cap is `capability − floor`, so as `reachPractice` walks capability up, more of the authored price survives, more cards differentiate, and `perilous` becomes reachable — the card reports risk exactly when risk becomes real, with no re-tune and **no template re-pricing** (the THR-736 anti-pattern). Direction 3 stays ruled out — those floors govern mortal resolution too. **The pinned "difficulty is inert" assertion stays green, deliberately**: its header said it "must go red when THR-998 lands", which assumed direction 3; the engine property is real and unchanged, and what was removed is the *card* reporting it as a per-template risk — header and inline comment corrected rather than left to rot. THR-1068 excluded legacy steps defensively (a resolved legacy record drops out of the dedup key set, so expiring one would re-emit it next tick); THR-1069 asked the prior question and found **the branch unreachable by construction**. `phaseAgentDecision` takes its legacy arm only on `template && !unifiedTemplate`, but `getUnifiedTemplateById` is `index.get(id) ?? getAnyEncounterById(id)` — a **strict superset** of the lookup producing `template` — so the first arm always wins. The other two writers of `state.encounterProgress` are inert too: `initiateEncounter` has **zero production callers**, and `debugEncounterTools`' `legacy` mode is gated on the identical impossible condition. **The empirical arm carries a control, because without one it would be worthless**: a 60-tick sweep (`--seed 42 --map medium`) recorded `encounterProgress = 0` *alongside* 52 unified actions across 33 distinct templates, proving agents acted throughout — while the same run's notification counts are **not** usable evidence, the CLI seed carrying no ascendant thread so `phaseEncounterVisibility` returns early and every notification reading is a vacuous empty-population pass. **Pinned rather than pruned, against the ticket's own suggested outcome**, for two measured reasons: the unreachability rests on a single trailing `??` that **36 of 260 pool ids depend on** (they are in no unified pool — delete it and the dead arm goes live for exactly those, making THR-1068's churn loop real), and `phaseEncounterVisibility.test.ts` builds its states from `encounterProgress`, so a prune deletes that file's subject — a poor trade against NFP #6 for code that is inert rather than blocking. New `legacyEncounterBranchUnreachable.test.ts` asserts the branch condition over the whole corpus, floors the population at 200 ids so it cannot pass vacuously, and pins the fallback as load-bearing; **falsified** by removing the `??`, which turns two assertions red. Three comment sites carrying the speculative justification now carry the proven one — including the dedup filter, the silence the ticket actually named. Noted and left alone: the two lookups return **different objects** for 83 ids, a real duplication outside this scope. 994 files / 15,903 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3447, build clean, smoke to tick 30 with 383 agents.
- ✅ **THR-1033** (2026-08-12) — the Aftermath screen's consequence chips underlined concept words that explained nothing, and the cause was not the renderer THR-986 suspected. THR-1004 had already wired the chip surface correctly; what shipped broken were **the ids the producers hand it**. `aftermathWords.ts` emitted `tooltipId: 'ui.reputation'` for every personal-standing sentence and that id has never existed — the registry entry is `ui.standing` — so **every STANDING chip in the game** carried an unresolvable id. `reachTooltipId` offered `reach.time` and `reach.life` because `REACH_DISPLAY_NAMES` holds eleven display words against `world-model.json`'s nine `reach.*` nodes, and a nudge fixture declared `condition.exhausted`, a prefix `resolveTooltip` does not route at all. **The two failures compose into the lie**: `Tooltip` no-ops silently on an unresolvable id, while the chip drew its underline on the mere *presence* of a `tooltipId` — a dead link that looks live, the anti-pattern Law 21 names by hand. **The ticket's own DOM probe was a false negative and that mattered**: it searched for `role`/`tabindex`/`title`/`data-tip`, none of which this `Tooltip` implementation ever sets, so it reported "nothing wired" for the MARK chips whose `reach.eye`/`reach.star` ids resolve perfectly — verifying the noun before the verb is what separated the three genuinely-dangling ids from the four working ones. Fixed at the source, **and** at the surface: new `tooltipResolves()` mirrors `Tooltip`'s own `hasContent` gate, so a word is styled as explainable exactly when hovering it would explain something and a future dangling id degrades to plain prose instead of to a lie. A resolvable word additionally takes `tabIndex={0}` + `.focus-ring`, making the hover tier keyboard-reachable at this call site. **The missing gate was the real finding**: `tooltipValidation.test.ts` checked only `{{concept.id}}` links *inside* descriptions and never looked at producer-emitted ids, which is precisely the gap `ui.reputation` fell through — new `conceptTooltipIds.test.ts` sweeps every `tooltipId:` literal under `src/` as a corpus, not a fixture list, and **caught the `condition.exhausted` fixture on its first run**. Falsified in both directions before shipping. Two deferrals filed with their reasons rather than folded in: THR-1094 (should a condition explain itself on hover — a registry-design call needing authored copy) and THR-1095 (the shared `Tooltip` trigger's focus path is dead code game-wide; making every tooltip a tab stop is a decision with a blast radius). 995 files / 15,912 tests green, ratchet unchanged at 3447, build clean. **Browser-verify substituted, pixel capture owed** — impediment #546 second occurrence.
- ✅ **THR-1098** (2026-08-12) — SCAR / BOND / BOON / PATH seated as canonical terms in the Encounters UL shard, the four story-first consequence categories replacing the six aftermath display kinds. **They are UL words rather than display copy because they graduate at birth**: encounter authors declare `category` per the nudge authoring spec in the same PR that introduces them, so the vocabulary crosses engine payload, authoring spec and UI immediately — the intent-judge finding that a conditional "file it if they graduate" was wrong. **Each of the four landed on a word this shard already owns, so each carries its own collision note**: the retired `MARK` display kind is not `[[Hidden Mark]]` (hidden marks and curse marks are live engine concepts, untouched); **BOND** is neither `[[Bond Reception]]` — how a mortal receives the *god* at the Meet-The-First climax — nor `bondQuality`, so three senses of *bond* now coexist and a BOND chip never reports the god↔mortal thread; **PATH** is not `[[Encounter Seed]]`, the engine object a PATH chip usually reports the planting of. **`THREAD` is recorded as rejected** for the fourth category, because the design brainstorm makes it read well and a later session would otherwise revive it against the UL's most load-bearing word. **MARK's deletion is written up as load-bearing, not incidental** — it was the "everything else" bucket, and there is deliberately no fifth catch-all: an unclassifiable change folds by polarity (`loss`/`mixed` → SCAR, `gain` → BOON, `info` → PATH), never to a blank. **Two footer counts were stale and are now measured rather than asserted:** the v1.7 line read "117 canonical + 1 rejected + 2 deprecated", correct on canonical but silently dropping the one `proposed` term (Rebuild Road) for an implied 120 against an actual 121, while index coverage still claimed "118 of 118" against 121 headings; both now read 125, verified by the THR-806 shard-vs-index diff run through the repo's own `slugifyHeading` — **125 headings, 125 anchors, no unindexed terms, no dead anchors**. The footer now also says to count *every* `**Status:**` line rather than the statuses you expect, since that is the specific error and it has now been made twice in different forms. **One trap found and written down** (impediment #548): a hand-rolled slugifier reports the two Graph versioning entries as both unindexed and dead-anchored — a false positive on the one pair the footer records as already repaired, because `slugifyHeading` collapses repeated hyphens and an ad-hoc implementation does not. Not blocked on THR-1082 by its own terms; PR #1415 is held pending an attended pixel pass and does not gate the vocabulary. Docs-only diff (THR-917 predicate empty), closed out on the docs track.
